pt_psse.headline: The engine's convex/concave derivation is correct, but the library then applies it inconsistently: the sitting waist fold is cued INTO the curve for thoracic patients, child's pose has an inverted rationale, "frog in the pond" is an unsourced single-patient exercise never mirrored for left curves, and side-plank-wrong-side is called an ABSOLUTE contraindication on the strength of one uncontrolled yoga case series while the product's own outcome measure requires bilateral side bridges. Nothing in the library is actually a Schroth or SEAS exercise; the PSSE core (pelvic corrections, elongation, 3D autocorrection, stabilisation, ADL integration) is absent, so the "Schroth" labelling is exposure, not substance.

findings.area: library.ts — sitting_waist_fold (Tier 3)
findings.claim_in_product: asymmetric_cues.right_thoracic: "Fold to the left to open the right concave thoracic side." and left_thoracic: "Fold to the right to open the left concave thoracic side." Description: "fold left waist (compresses left side, opens right)."
findings.problem: A right thoracic curve is convex right and concave LEFT (profile.ts derives this correctly, and schroth_rotational_breathing in the same file says so: "Inhale into the LEFT ribs to open the concave side"). The waist-fold cue labels the RIGHT side as concave, then tells the patient to side-bend LEFT — which compresses the already-shortened left concave ribs and opens the right convexity. That is lateral flexion in the direction of the deformity: the exercise reinforces the curve for every thoracic pattern, and the two Tier-3/Tier-5 items contradict each other about which side is concave. The most likely origin is that the cue was transcribed from one patient's programme where "fold left" was a LUMBAR correction (left lumbar curve in a right-thoracic/left-lumbar S: side-bending left toward the lumbar convexity opens the right lumbar concavity) and then mis-keyed to the thoracic curve.
findings.correction: Fix the labels and direction now: for right_thoracic the corrective lateral flexion is to the RIGHT (toward the convexity, opening the left concave side); mirror for left_thoracic. If the intent was a lumbar correction, key it on lumbar patterns (left_lumbar → fold left; right_lumbar → fold right; double_RT_LL → fold left labelled as lumbar) and drop the thoracic keys. Better still, replace a pure side-bend with the Schroth/SEAS form: elongation first, then a lateral TRANSLATION of the thoracic block toward the concave side with a concave-side breath, and never let "open the convex side" appear anywhere. Add a unit test that asserts, for every exercise, that any cue containing "concave" agrees with deriveRegionalSides(); this contradiction would have been caught mechanically.
findings.evidence: Convention: curve named by side of convexity (SRS glossary; Lehnert-Schroth, Three-Dimensional Treatment for Scoliosis). Schroth corrections always open the concavity and never side-bend toward the concave side; SEAS active self-correction likewise moves the trunk away from the deformity (Berdishevsky et al., Scoliosis Spinal Disord 2016, seven-schools review). The internal inconsistency is verifiable directly in library.ts lines 224–233 vs 361–362.

findings.area: contraindications.ts checkSidePlankSide (category: "absolute") + library side_plank_convex_thoracic_side_down + selectProgram physio_cleared side check
findings.claim_in_product: "Side plank should be done with your [convex] side down… Holding the other side reinforces the curve." Wrong-side side plank is an ABSOLUTE contraindication; library description says "Wrong side held long is a contraindication."
findings.problem: Convex-side-down side plank is the Fishman yoga protocol, not PSSE. Its evidence is a single uncontrolled serial case series (25 patients, mixed idiopathic and degenerative, self-selected compliance, radiographs read by the authors, mean ~1.5 min/day) reporting Cobb improvement; it has never been replicated in a controlled trial, and no study shows that the opposite-side plank worsens a curve. Mainstream PSSE (Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS) does not prescribe the unilateral plank as a corrective and most Schroth clinicians would question the rationale (the concave-side trunk musculature is the shortened/underactive side). Calling the non-convex side an ABSOLUTE contraindication (same tier as inversions) is indefensible clinically — and it contradicts the product's own outcomes module, which measures McGill side-bridge endurance LEFT and RIGHT and calls a ratio: the patient cannot perform that test without doing the "contraindicated" side. For a physio who prescribes bilateral side planks (standard in trunk-endurance programmes), the app will flag their prescription with a strong red warning and an "unsafe" label in the handoff PDF.
findings.correction: Downgrade to a cue preference, not a contraindication: keep the convex-side-down bias as an optional asymmetry ("we do a little longer on the [convex] side" — say why and say the evidence is preliminary), allow bilateral side bridge as the default, and remove the "reinforces the curve" sentence entirely. Delete the `absolute` category from checkSidePlankSide (make it informational), and make the side-bridge endurance outcome test explicitly bilateral in the UI. In the clinician handoff, describe the asymmetry as "Fishman-style convex-side bias, preliminary evidence" so a Schroth-trained physio knows what they're looking at. For double curves, state which curve the bias follows (primary/larger) rather than always thoracic.
findings.evidence: Fishman LM, Groessl EJ, Sherman KJ. Serial case reporting yoga for idiopathic and degenerative scoliosis. Glob Adv Health Med 2014;3(5):16–21 — case series, no control group. No PSSE guideline (SOSORT 2016, Negrini et al. 2018) lists a unilateral side plank as either prescribed or contraindicated. Bilateral side-bridge endurance norms and L/R ratio: McGill, Childs, Liebenson, Arch Phys Med Rehabil 1999 (the same convention the outcomes module cites). Contradiction with lib/outcomes/compute.ts is verifiable in-repo.

findings.area: library.ts — frog_in_the_pond (Tier 3, applicable_patterns right_thoracic + double_RT_LL only)
findings.claim_in_product: "Lying down, knees bent left and parallel to mat line, left hand on neck, left scapula rotates back, right hand at 90°." Execution cues: "Scapular position, knee alignment to mat line." 3×30 s. Category derotation. Form target: scapular_position.
findings.problem: I cannot identify this as a named Schroth ("Frosch"/"Frosch am Teich") or SEAS element — I found no such exercise in the Schroth canon I teach from (muscle cylinder, door-frame, 50× exercise, side-lying/prone corrections etc.) and could not verify the name against a source, so treat that as UNVERIFIED rather than confirmed absent. Independently of the name, the description is not a coherent corrective as written: (1) there is no stated purpose, breath, elongation or pelvic correction — the "execution cues" are form-check targets, not instructions; (2) dropping the knees LEFT rotates the pelvis/lumbar spine to the left and pulling the LEFT scapula back rotates the thorax to the left as well, so thorax and pelvis rotate the same way — that is a whole-body roll, not the counter-rotation a derotation stretch relies on; (3) it exists only for right-thoracic patterns because it was transcribed from one patient's programme and never mirrored, so a left-thoracic patient (who the red-flag module already treats as atypical) gets one fewer Tier-3 exercise for no clinical reason; (4) "scapular_position" from a single webcam on a supine patient is not measurable.
findings.correction: Either source it or cut it. If it stays: write it as a real exercise (position, what to lengthen, where to breathe, what to hold, why), state the originating method or attribute it to "your physio's programme", and add the exact mirror for left_thoracic / double_LT_RL. Remove the form-check target. If the intent is a supine thoracic derotation for right thoracic, the standard PSSE version is: supine, elongate, concave-side (left) arm reaching overhead along the floor, breathe into the left posterior ribs, exhale and pull the right posterior rib hump forward/down toward the mat — with the pelvis STABLE, not dropped to one side.
findings.evidence: Schroth exercise inventory: Lehnert-Schroth C, Three-Dimensional Treatment for Scoliosis; Berdishevsky et al. 2016 seven-schools review. The name lookup is from memory and UNVERIFIED — I could not confirm or refute "Frosch am Teich" as a Schroth exercise. The biomechanical incoherence and unmirrored applicability are verifiable directly from library.ts lines 200–217.

findings.area: library.ts — childs_pose_side_reach (Tier 4); also bird_dog_asymmetric_hold rationale wording
findings.claim_in_product: "Reach toward convex thoracic side to lengthen it." right_thoracic: "Longer reach to the right (convex thoracic side)." Bird-dog right_thoracic: "Longer hold extending the left arm + right leg (opens the left concave side)."
findings.problem: Two errors that happen to cancel. (1) Biomechanics: in child's pose, walking BOTH hands to the right side-bends the trunk to the right; that lengthens the LEFT lateral trunk and shortens the right. So "reach right to lengthen the right side" is backwards — reaching right lengthens the left. (2) Principle: PSSE never sets out to lengthen the CONVEX side; the convex side is already the long/overstretched side and the goal is to open and elongate the CONCAVE side (and derotate). Because right thoracic is concave left, reaching right does lengthen the concave left side — the ACTION is correct, the RATIONALE is doubly wrong, and any Schroth-trained physio reading "lengthen the convex side" in the handoff PDF will stop trusting the rest. Bird-dog is different and is defensible: a UNILATERAL overhead arm reach with the trunk fixed lengthens the ipsilateral lateral trunk/latissimus, and lifting the left arm in quadruped tends to draw the left shoulder up and back, i.e. left thoracic rotation, which is the derotation direction for a right thoracic curve (vertebral bodies rotated right, posterior hump right). "Opens the left concave side" is a modest but reasonable claim there. The app must not, however, use the same "reach side = lengthened side" logic for a bilateral side-walk, which is what child's pose is.
findings.correction: Rewrite child's pose: "Walk both hands toward your [convex, right] side so the trunk bends right — this opens and lengthens the [concave, left] ribs. Breathe into the left ribs while you hold." Keep the direction, fix every word about which side is being lengthened. Add the same concave-side breath cue to the bird-dog long hold and keep its side assignment. Add a short glossary line in the handoff PDF stating the convention ("right thoracic = convex right, concave left") so clinicians can check the cues at a glance.
findings.evidence: Lateral flexion lengthens the contralateral trunk — basic kinesiology (Kendall & McCreary; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System). Schroth principle of opening/elongating the concavity and derotating the convex-side posterior ribs: Lehnert-Schroth; Weiss HR, Schroth method literature; Berdishevsky et al. 2016. Cue text verifiable at library.ts lines 331–340 and 165–170.

findings.area: library.ts — schroth_rotational_breathing (Tier 5) and selectProgram tier bias (pain → [4,5,1,2,3])
findings.claim_in_product: "Schroth rotational breathing … Seated or side-lying, hands placed over the concave ribs. Breathe into the concave side(s) to expand collapsed ribs." right_thoracic → "Inhale into the left ribs." 3×10.
findings.problem: Direction is correct and this is the one genuinely Schroth element in the library — but it is presented as a stand-alone 30-breath drill. In Schroth, rotational angular breathing (RAB) is never the first step: it is performed only after (a) pelvic corrections, (b) elongation/axial extension, (c) lateral translation/derotation of the trunk blocks are established, and it is completed by (d) isometric tension on the exhale to STABILISE the corrected position. Without those, 3×10 breaths seated in the habitual collapsed posture mostly move air, not ribs. The breathing target is also only half-described: for a right thoracic curve RAB directs the breath into the LEFT POSTERIOR concave ribs AND the RIGHT ANTERIOR chest (the anterior concavity paired with the posterior rib hump) to produce derotation; "left ribs" alone omits the derotational half. For S-curves the lumbar concavity (the right waist for a left lumbar curve) needs its own target, which the cues don't specify. Prescribing it as a fallback for pain days is fine; prescribing it as the sole "Schroth" content while using the trademarked name is not.
findings.correction: Make RAB a sequence, not a drill: (1) sit tall on the front of a chair, feet flat, pelvis level — 30 s; (2) elongate ("grow tall from the crown, chin level"); (3) shift the rib cage gently toward the [concave] side; (4) inhale into the [concave] posterior ribs and the [convex-side] front of the chest; (5) exhale slowly and tighten the trunk to hold the taller position; 3×10 breaths with a mirror or a hand on each target. Cue lumbar targets separately for double patterns. Rename to "rotational breathing (Schroth-style)" unless certified content is licensed.
findings.evidence: Schroth RAB and the correction sequence: Lehnert-Schroth C, Three-Dimensional Treatment for Scoliosis; Weiss HR (multiple); Berdishevsky et al. 2016 describes RAB explicitly as a component following pelvic corrections and elongation. Schreiber S et al., Scoliosis 2015 and PLoS One 2016 (Schroth RCTs) delivered full 3D-correction programmes with supervised sessions plus 30–45 min/day home practice — not isolated breathing.

findings.area: contraindications.ts CONTRAINDICATION_RULES (absolute tier) and the absence of population-specific rules
findings.claim_in_product: ABSOLUTE: full backbends ("extreme load on the convex side"), deadlifts/RDL ("amplify rotational forces"), loaded forward flexion incl. Pilates roll-up ("compress the spine in flexion — bad news for asymmetric loading"), end-range static twists ("pull the spine into existing rotation"), inversions ("stack asymmetric loads unpredictably").
findings.problem: None of the five absolute rules is evidence-based for idiopathic scoliosis. SOSORT guidelines explicitly encourage sport and general physical activity for AIS and adult IS; there is no trial showing deadlifts, backbends, seated twists or inversions progress a curve, and the mechanistic rationales given ("extreme load on the convex side", "amplify rotational forces") are folk wisdom. A seated spinal twist held 30 s is a routine mobility exercise; a Pilates roll-up is unloaded and is matched by a rule titled "loaded" flexion; a supervised hinge/deadlift is standard strength training for a young adult with a 25° curve. The deadlift rule is internally inconsistent — its copy says "only if your physio has cleared it", which is the definition of the product's own RELATIVE tier, yet it is tagged absolute and will red-flag a physio's programme. Meanwhile the populations for whom exercise contraindications are REAL are absent: post-fusion patients (no end-range flexion/extension/rotation through fused levels, surgeon-set timelines, no contact loading early — the app has no fusion pathway at all), osteoporotic adults with degenerative scoliosis (loaded/end-range flexion IS contraindicated — fracture risk), spondylolisthesis, pregnancy, and active inflammatory/neurological red flags (already handled separately, correctly). A clinician will read the absolute list as amateur and the missing list as unsafe.
findings.correction: Reclassify: nothing in idiopathic scoliosis outside red flags is absolute. Move backbends, deadlifts, twists, inversions and loaded flexion to "ask_physio" (or relative with honest wording: "not harmful in itself; we don't auto-prescribe it — your physio decides"). Rewrite reasons without mechanistic claims you cannot cite; remove "roll-up" from the loaded-flexion regex. Add the rules that matter: (1) a `spinal_fusion: true` profile flag that suppresses every end-range flexion/rotation/extension item and all side-bends (sitting_waist_fold, childs_pose_side_reach, frog) and forces physio_cleared mode; (2) `osteoporosis/age>60 + degenerative` → loaded flexion and end-range flexion become genuinely contraindicated (the only place that rule belongs); (3) pregnancy → no prone/supine-long holds after ~20 weeks, no Valsalva; (4) known spondylolisthesis → no repeated end-range extension. Keep the >60 s asymmetric hold rule as relative — that one is reasonable.
findings.evidence: SOSORT 2016 guidelines (Negrini S et al., Scoliosis Spinal Disord 2018;13:3): sport and general activity recommended in IS; no exercise categories listed as contraindicated. Osteoporosis + flexion: Sinaki M, Mikkelsen BA, Arch Phys Med Rehabil 1984 (flexion exercises associated with vertebral fractures). Post-fusion precautions are surgeon-protocol based (UNVERIFIED as to any single citation; standard practice). Rule text and category tags verifiable at contraindications.ts lines 40–117.

findings.area: library.ts tier design, selectProgram tier labels ("Schroth-adjacent corrective"), agent prompts, handoff PDF
findings.claim_in_product: Tier 3 labelled "Schroth-adjacent corrective"; Tier 5 named "Schroth rotational breathing"; the programme is positioned as scoliosis-specific home exercise with physio handoff.
findings.problem: Exercise by exercise: hip bridge, single-leg bridge, pelvic mobility drill, foam roller, clam, lunge, T-stretch, bird-dog, squat, hip-flexor stretch, wall stand, cat-cow and child's pose are generic core/hip/mobility exercises with an asymmetric cue bolted on (several cues — "front leg feels almost nothing", "press the convex-lumbar pelvis down" — are one patient's individualised physio instructions generalised to everyone, without a stated mechanism). Not one item is a recognised Schroth, BSPTS or SEAS exercise; the two that gesture at PSSE (waist fold, frog) are miscued or unsourced (see other findings). Everything that DEFINES PSSE is missing: (a) Rigo/Schroth curve classification (3C/3CH/3CTL/4C) driving exercise choice — the app has right/left thoracic/lumbar/thoracolumbar only, with no pelvis-in/out-of-curve distinction; (b) the five Schroth pelvic corrections as the starting position of every exercise; (c) elongation/axial extension; (d) 3D active self-correction (SEAS's entire method) taught with a mirror and tactile feedback; (e) stabilisation of the corrected posture by isometric tension; (f) integration into ADLs (sitting, standing, walking, sleeping positions) — the wall stand is the only nod; (g) progression criteria (hold time in correction, quality, independence from mirror) — tiers are re-picked daily from pain and scan data instead; (h) home dosage per SOSORT/Schroth practice — supervised sessions plus daily home practice in the 20–45 min range for months, not 3–5 items chosen by a tier permutation; (i) brace-wear integration for the adolescent cohort you plan to serve (PSSE around brace hours is the core of adolescent management). A physio receiving the handoff PDF will see a glute/core programme wearing a Schroth name — and "Schroth" is a trademarked, certified method (your own product-strategy doc flags this).
findings.correction: Be honest first: rename Tier 3 "corrective (side-specific)" and Tier 5 "rotational breathing (Schroth-inspired)" until you have certified content; state in onboarding and the PDF that the self-guided library is a conditioning/adherence programme and that PSSE is delivered by the physio. Then build the missing spine: (1) a mandatory 90-second "corrected posture" block (pelvic level → elongate → shift toward concave → breathe into concave → hold on exhale) that precedes every session and is the thing the mirror/webcam actually watches; (2) extend the curve model with pelvis-in/out-of-curve and a thoracolumbar/lumbar distinction so exercises can be keyed on a Rigo-style type; (3) replace the pain/scan tier permutation with progression criteria (corrected-hold seconds, form quality, days adherent) for the self-guided path, and let the physio set dosage explicitly; (4) add a brace-hours field and schedule exercises around it before any adolescent launch; (5) use the LLM agents for adherence and reflection only — never to invent asymmetric cues.
findings.evidence: Berdishevsky H et al. Physiotherapy scoliosis-specific exercises – a comprehensive review of seven major schools. Scoliosis Spinal Disord 2016;11:20 (defines PSSE components: 3D autocorrection, ADL training, stabilisation, patient education). Rigo M, Villagrasa M, Gallo D. A specific scoliosis classification correlating with brace treatment. Scoliosis 2010;5:1. SEAS active self-correction: Monticone M et al., Eur Spine J 2014 (RCT); Romano M et al. SEAS description, Scoliosis 2015. Schroth home dosage: Schreiber et al. 2015/2016 used supervised sessions plus a daily home programme (exact minutes UNVERIFIED from memory, order of 30–45 min). SOSORT 2016 guidelines on PSSE and bracing integration. Trademark note verifiable in docs/product-strategy.html line 701.

findings.area: lib/exercises/formCheck/* (birdDog, hipBridge, sidePlank, lunge, tStretch) and form_check_targets in library.ts
findings.claim_in_product: Bird dog: hip drop >0.018, "spine rotation" >0.25 rad shoulder-vs-hip line → cue "Square your shoulders to your hips — no twist." Hip bridge: uneven lift, knees collapsed, partial range. Side plank: sag/pike, shoulder roll, head drop. Lunge: knee valgus, uneven hips; pelvic tilt out of scope. T-stretch: horizontal ratio, hip rotation.
findings.problem: The compensations detected are standard fitness-form compensations (hip sag, knee valgus, uneven lift) — sensible for injury-avoidance coaching, but none of them is the compensation a PSSE clinician watches for. The scoliosis-relevant faults are: loss of elongation (collapsing back into the curve during the hold), trunk translating back toward the convex side, convex-side shoulder girdle dropping/rolling forward, rib hump increasing on exertion, breath going into the convex side, and pelvis shifting laterally — none is checked, and several are genuinely not visible from one webcam, which the team should say plainly. Worse, the bird-dog check treats ANY shoulder-hip line mismatch as a fault to be corrected ("no twist"), whereas a controlled derotation toward the concave side is precisely what the long hold is supposed to encourage; the cue will fight the intended correction on the cued side. The fixed normalised thresholds (0.018 hip y-diff, 0.25 rad) are also camera-angle dependent — a three-quarter view produces apparent "rotation" with no rotation at all. And the "wrong_side" soft nudge ("do the other side a little longer; that's the one we want") fires on the NON-cued side even though the exercise is prescribed per side, so on every alternate rep the patient is told they are on the wrong side.
findings.correction: Reposition the form check as a SAFETY monitor (sag, valgus, partial range, falling out of position) and stop presenting it as corrective-quality feedback. Remove the bird-dog "no twist" cue on the cued-side hold (or make it a rotation-away-from-correction check only). Silence the "wrong side" nudge — both sides are prescribed; only the hold-duration target differs. Where you keep angular thresholds, gate them on a camera-setup check (frontal vs oblique) or use the scale-invariant angles the pose module already exposes. If you ever want a scoliosis-relevant check, the one measurable from a webcam is torso height/elongation and lateral trunk-midline offset during the corrected-posture block (see the PSSE finding) — trend it per user against their own baseline, exactly as the outcomes module already does for MDC.
findings.evidence: Clinical reasoning from PSSE practice (Schroth/SEAS emphasise maintenance of correction, elongation and derotation over generic alignment). No published normative thresholds exist for webcam-derived compensation cut-offs in scoliosis; the thresholds are engineering choices (UNVERIFIED as to any clinical validation). Behaviour verifiable in formCheck/birdDog.ts lines 174–187 and 267–284.

things_done_right: profile.ts derives convexity correctly and in the user's own words ("which way does your back bulge" = convex/lean side; concave = opposite), and deriveRegionalSides handles thoracic and lumbar separately for S-curves. This is the right foundation — the errors are downstream in cue text, not in the model.
selectProgram withholds every side-specific exercise when convexity is unknown rather than guessing. That is exactly what a PSSE clinician would do; keep it.
schroth_rotational_breathing has the correct direction (right thoracic → inhale into the LEFT/concave ribs) and correctly notes separate targets per curve in S-patterns.

bird_dog_asymmetric_hold assigns the correct arm (concave-side arm, i.e. LEFT arm for right thoracic) for a longer hold; the biomechanics are defensible (ipsilateral lateral-trunk lengthening plus a left-rotation tendency that matches the derotation direction for a right thoracic curve).
childs_pose_side_reach's ACTION direction (reach right for right thoracic) is correct even though its rationale is inverted — fix the words, keep the movement.
The relative rule on asymmetric static holds >60 s is sensible and matches how PSSE clinicians actually dose asymmetric positions (short, frequent, in correction).

Physio prescription is authoritative in physio_cleared mode and is never blocked, only flagged; the self-guided path never auto-prescribes relative items. That hierarchy is correct and should survive every other change.

The red-flag screen is clinically sound: cauda equina and progressive neurological deficit correctly block the session; left thoracic curve under 18 is correctly a review flag (atypical pattern → consider MRI); night pain, weight loss, cancer history and trauma are the right urgent items; questions are phrased so "yes" flags, and copy never names a condition.

The LLM safety floor (fixed template, never suggest exercise on neuro/bladder/bowel symptoms, exercise suggestions restricted to the fixed library, name redaction) is the right design for an agent in a clinical product.

Dosages in the library are plausible for a home programme (3×30 s side plank, 3×10 bridges, 8/side bird-dog, 2×45 s hip flexor, 3×10 RAB) — none is unsafe as a load; the problem is content and cueing, not volume.
Coaching hygiene in the form check is good: a compensation must persist 2 s before a cue and cues are rate-limited to one per 5 s; hold timers pause when out of position rather than resetting.

The team's own demotion of the webcam posture scan ("cannot measure Cobb or progression; qualitative photo only") and the MDC-gated posture trends (SEM = SD_diff/√2, MDC95 = 1.96·SD_diff, ≥5 pairs) are exactly the epistemic honesty a clinician wants to see. Side-bridge L/R endurance and PSFS with stated MCIDs are appropriate outcome measures — keep them (and let them force the side-plank contraindication fix).
The X-ray report parse requires field-by-field user confirmation before it is saved, and the ATR inclinometer never returns zero when no sensor exists. Both are correct safety defaults.

surgeon.headline: The engineering discipline is good (red-flag tiers, MDC gating, honest demotion of the webcam scan), but the clinical layer has one flatly backwards corrective cue, a single-point-of-failure way of learning convexity (self-reported "bulge", or an LLM reading an X-ray photo), a red-flag screen that misses the scoliosis-specific referrals (neural-axis soft signs, post-fusion, congenital/NF1, skeletal-maturity/bracing window, stenosis), and "cascade" chains that have no clinical basis and imply progression detection from a sensor the team already knows cannot detect it.

findings.area: lib/exercises/library.ts — sitting_waist_fold, childs_pose_side_reach (concave/convex convention)
findings.claim_in_product: sitting_waist_fold: right_thoracic -> "Fold to the left to open the right concave thoracic side"; left_thoracic -> "Fold to the right to open the left concave thoracic side". Description hard-codes "fold left waist (compresses left side, opens right)" on an 'any'-pattern exercise. childs_pose_side_reach: "Reach toward convex thoracic side to LENGTHEN it… right_thoracic -> longer reach right (convex thoracic side)".
findings.problem: Definitive convention: a curve is named for the side of its CONVEXITY. A right thoracic curve is convex right, so the concave (collapsed, short) side is LEFT — which is exactly what schroth_rotational_breathing and bird_dog_asymmetric_hold already say. sitting_waist_fold says the opposite (concave = right) AND its movement is backwards: by its own description folding left compresses the left side, i.e. it closes the concavity of a right thoracic curve and exaggerates the deformity — the one thing a corrective side-bend must never do. This is the founder's own pattern (RT + LL demo profile) leaking in: fold-left IS corrective for the LEFT LUMBAR component (convex left, concave right), but the cue is keyed to right_thoracic and labelled thoracic. childs_pose_side_reach moves in the right direction by accident but its rationale is inverted — the convex side is already the long side; nobody lengthens the convexity. Every side-keyed cue audited: CORRECT — schroth_rotational_breathing (RT -> inhale left), bird_dog_asymmetric_hold (RT -> left arm/right leg, 'opens left concave'), side_plank_convex_thoracic_side_down (RT -> right down), frog_in_the_pond (pattern-gated). BACKWARDS — sitting_waist_fold (both cues + description). WRONG RATIONALE, RIGHT DIRECTION — childs_pose_side_reach. UNGROUNDED, NOT DEMONSTRABLY WRONG — hip_bridge_pelvic_press_down / single_leg_bridge_variant 'press convex-lumbar pelvis down' (no PSSE school I know cues this; leave to the physio).
findings.correction: Adopt one rule everywhere and encode it as a helper (foldToward(curve) = convexSide(curve)): 'A corrective lateral fold goes TOWARD the convexity of the curve being targeted, so the concavity opens.' Then: sitting_waist_fold right_thoracic -> 'Fold to the RIGHT so the LEFT (concave) thoracic side lengthens'; left_thoracic -> fold LEFT. Because a waist fold acts mostly on the lumbar/thoracolumbar segment, add lumbar keys (left_lumbar -> fold left, right_lumbar -> fold right) and for double curves drive it from the lumbar convexity, not the thoracic, with a note that the thoracic must be held stable (or drop the exercise from self-guided for S-curves). Delete the hard-coded 'fold left' description. childs_pose_side_reach: keep the direction, rewrite rationale to 'reach toward the convex side so the concave side lengthens'. Add a unit test that asserts, for every asymmetric_cues entry, that any string containing 'concave' names opposite(convexSide) and any containing 'convex' names convexSide — that test would have caught this. Soften side-plank 'wrong side is a contraindication' to 'not the cued side' (see contraindications finding).
findings.evidence: Naming convention (curve named by convexity; concavity is the short, rib-collapsed side) is universal in scoliosis texts and SRS terminology. Schroth/PSSE corrective side-bending elongates the concavity (Lehnert-Schroth; Weiss). Internal evidence: the codebase's own profile.ts line 28 states 'Concave side = opposite of lean', so the waist-fold cue contradicts the product's own model. Fishman 2014 side plank convex-side-down — UNVERIFIED from memory but consistent with the library.

findings.area: lib/exercises/profile.ts (primaryLeanSide / deriveRegionalSides) + app/profile/page.tsx 'Primary bulges to' + app/page.tsx '· right lean'
findings.claim_in_product: Convexity is taken from the user's answer to 'Primary bulges to: left | right' (internally 'lean side = the side the back bulges toward = the convex side') and then drives every side-keyed cue, the side-plank contraindication check, bird-dog long-hold side and the ATR sign interpretation.
findings.problem: For THORACIC curves the posterior rib hump is on the convex side, so 'bulge' mostly works. For LUMBAR and thoracolumbar curves it fails systematically: what the patient sees and feels as the 'bulge' is the prominent hip and flank, which sits on the CONCAVE side of a lumbar curve (a left lumbar curve presents with a prominent right hip and deeper left waist crease). Patients also report shoulder height, waist asymmetry or where they 'lean' — coronal trunk shift is toward the convexity in some and away in decompensated adults — so the word 'lean' is ambiguous and the UI label '· right lean' (app/page.tsx:412) will be read as trunk list, not convexity. One wrong tap silently inverts every corrective in the programme and turns the side-plank 'contraindication' check into a rule that enforces the wrong side. There is no cross-check against the ATR sign, the X-ray, or the physio's notes, and 'unknown' is not offered on the bulge chips (only left/right), so unsure users are forced to guess.
findings.correction: 1) Add 'Not sure' to the bulge chips; unsure -> pattern 'any' (side cues withheld), which the engine already handles well. 2) Ask the question per curve in the forward-bend position with a picture: 'Bend forward. Which side of your back is higher/humped?' — the Adams posterior prominence is convex-side for both thoracic and lumbar curves; explicitly warn 'not the hip that sticks out'. 3) Cross-check: if ATR peak sign, X-ray convex_side and self-report disagree, downgrade to 'any' and ask the physio to confirm in the handoff PDF. 4) Prefer the radiology REPORT wording ('convex to the right', 'dextroscoliosis'/'levoscoliosis') over any visual judgement. 5) Rename 'lean' to 'convex side' in the data model and UI copy. 6) In physio_cleared mode let the physio's stated pattern override the patient's self-report, not just the exercise list.
findings.evidence: Clinical examination convention: waist-crease asymmetry and hip prominence lie on the concave side of the lumbar curve; the Adams forward-bend prominence lies on the convex side (standard surgical examination teaching, e.g. Lovell & Winter; SRS patient examination guidance). Clinical reasoning for the ambiguity of 'lean'. UNVERIFIED as to published rates of patient laterality error — none known to me.

findings.area: lib/prompts/xray.ts (Gemini X-ray reader) + onboarding confirm step
findings.claim_in_product: The digest describes a 'Gemini-parsed X-ray REPORT', but the prompt actually reads an uploaded X-ray IMAGE and asks the model to output convex_side, apex_region, curve_type, a segmental_shift_impression, rotation_visible and an 'estimated_cobb_range' from a 'non-calibrated digital image'. The user confirms field-by-field.
findings.problem: Harm modes that survive user confirmation: (a) LATERALITY — a phone photo of a screen or lightbox, a mirrored selfie-camera capture, or a film displayed AP vs PA can flip left/right; PACS displays are conventionally shown as if facing the patient (patient's right on viewer's left) and side markers are often cropped. A flipped convex_side inverts every side-keyed cue, and the patient cannot verify it — they are confirming something they cannot check, so 'confirmation' is theatre. (b) COBB FROM A PHOTO — an uncalibrated, possibly rotated, possibly obliquely photographed image yields angle estimates that are wrong by well over 5°; that number lands in the severity bucket (Mild <25 / Moderate 25–40 / Severe >40), the progress page and the physio PDF. A falsely low range shown to a growing adolescent near the bracing threshold, or a falsely high one causing alarm, is real harm; an LLM 'range' also creates a paper trail that looks like a measurement. (c) ANCHORING — pre-filled values are accepted far more often than blank fields, so this step converts model error into 'patient-confirmed' data. (d) The segmental_shift_impression from the image feeds inferStiffHipFlexorSide, laundering an invented rule through an AI reading. (e) A lateral film may be accepted as coronal, or a non-scoliosis pathology (fracture, tumour, hemivertebra) passed over silently.
findings.correction: Switch the primary path to the radiology REPORT text or the physio's letter (measured Cobb angles, levels, 'convex right/left'); keep an image path only for reading the report photograph. If an image reader is retained: never output a Cobb estimate (return 'measured by radiologist only'); output convex_side only when a legible R/L marker is visible and state which marker was used, otherwise 'unclear'; drop segmental_shift_impression and rotation_visible; require the physio to sign off any image-derived convexity before it unlocks side-keyed cues (until then pattern = 'any'); label every AI-derived field 'AI-read, unverified' in the UI and the PDF; log the view_type and refuse lateral films. Add 'congenital anomaly / hardware / fracture visible' as an additional_observations trigger that routes to the red-flag REFER tier rather than being discarded.
findings.evidence: Radiographic display conventions (viewer-left = patient-right on standard coronal display) — standard radiology practice. Cobb inter-observer error on properly calibrated films is ~5° (Morrissy et al. JBJS 1990 — UNVERIFIED citation detail from memory); an uncalibrated phone photo cannot do better. Anchoring/automation bias: clinical reasoning, no specific citation offered.

findings.area: lib/safety/redFlags.ts — 9 rules / 9 onboarding questions
findings.claim_in_product: Emergency: cauda equina cluster; progressive leg weakness. Urgent: night pain; fever/weight loss; cancer history; trauma. Review: rapid curve change; left thoracic curve age <18 (derived); adult-onset curve. No surgical-history, maturity, syndromic, or leg-symptom questions.
findings.problem: This is a generic low-back-pain red-flag set, not a scoliosis one. Missing, with the disposition I would want: BLOCK self-guided mode (physio_cleared only): (1) prior spinal fusion or instrumentation — no post-fusion pathway exists, yet end-range twists, backbends, side-bending at the junctional level and 'de-rotation' cues above/below a fused segment are exactly what a fusion patient should not be self-prescribing; adjacent-segment or hardware pain needs a surgeon, not a coach; (2) diagnosed congenital, neuromuscular or syndromic scoliosis (incl. NF1, Marfan/EDS) — exercise is not a curve-modifying treatment for these and a dystrophic NF1 curve can progress fast. URGENT / REFER: (3) neural-axis soft signs a patient CAN self-report — headache or neck pain worsened by coughing/straining (Chiari), patches of numbness or burning, painless burns or cuts on hands/arms, hand clumsiness, one foot getting smaller/higher-arched or clawed toes, a hairy patch/dimple/lipoma over the spine (tethered cord), new bladder urgency short of retention; (4) significant back PAIN in an adolescent with scoliosis (AIS is usually painless; painful or stiff curves have a meaningful rate of underlying pathology — spondylolysis, osteoid osteoma, syrinx, tumour), and thoracic hyperkyphosis at the apex — the product has no sagittal-plane field at all so 'kyphotic scoliosis' can't fire; (5) juvenile onset (<10) — any curve, not just left thoracic, warrants MRI consideration; (6) adult neurogenic claudication (leg heaviness/pain on walking, relieved by sitting or leaning forward) and radicular leg pain below the knee — common in adult degenerative curves, and extension-biased items (wall_stand_postural_reset, bridging, t_stretch) can aggravate stenosis; (7) age >60 or known osteoporosis/prior fragility fracture with NEW acute back pain — vertebral fracture until proven otherwise; (8) NF1 stigmata in a child (≥6 café-au-lait spots, axillary freckling). REFER but do not block: (9) skeletal maturity — Risser 0–2 / pre-menarche / within a year of menarche with a curve ≥20–25° is a BRACING decision window; an app that keeps such a child exercising with no prompt to ask about bracing can quietly consume the window. ASK_PHYSIO only (fine as a gate, not a red flag): pregnancy (supine positioning after mid-pregnancy, ligamentous laxity), leg-length discrepancy. Fine to skip: Lenke/King classification, triple curves (route to physio_cleared).
findings.correction: Add onboarding questions for: prior spine surgery (-> physio_cleared only, and a post-fusion contraindication set: no end-range flexion/extension/rotation at junctional levels, no impact until surgeon clears); diagnosed congenital/neuromuscular/syndromic or NF1 (-> physio_cleared only + REFER); the neural-axis soft-sign cluster above (-> URGENT); adolescent significant pain or apex hyperkyphosis (-> REVIEW, MRI consideration); age at diagnosis <10 (-> REVIEW); walking-limited leg symptoms / leg pain below knee (-> URGENT if progressive, else ASK_PHYSIO + suppress extension-biased tier-4 items); >60 or osteoporosis with new acute pain (-> URGENT). For the HK adolescent cohort capture age, sex, menarche status, and self-reported recent growth spurt; if Cobb ≥20° and immature, surface 'ask your specialist about bracing' as a REVIEW flag and state that exercise is adjunctive. Keep the current 'yes raises a flag', condition-free copy style for all of these.
findings.evidence: MRI indications in scoliosis (left thoracic, juvenile onset, rapid progression, pain, neurological signs, apical kyphosis, absent abdominal reflexes) — standard texts and Davids et al. JBJS 2004 (UNVERIFIED citation detail). Back pain prevalence in AIS ~23% with ~9% of painful cases having identifiable pathology — Ramirez, Johnston & Browne, JBJS 1997 (from memory; UNVERIFIED numbers). Bracing efficacy in immature 20–40° curves — BrAIST, Weinstein et al., NEJM 2013. Post-fusion and degenerative stenosis reasoning is clinical, not from a guideline.

findings.area: lib/atr/compute.ts — bandFor 5°/7°, summarise (peak), rotationSide sign, gamma rejection, 4 fixed levels
findings.claim_in_product: Peak |deg| across four helper-chosen levels; ≥5° 'monitor' (HK school screening), ≥7° 'refer' (Bunnell); '+ = user's right side raised'; gamma >8° rejected as 'phone not flat'; copy tells a 'within' user their reading is 'below the 5° mark clinicians typically follow up on'.
findings.problem: The thresholds themselves are defensible screening cut-offs, but they are SCREENING numbers being shown to people who ALREADY HAVE diagnosed scoliosis — the product's actual users. For a known 30° curve, 'below the mark clinicians follow up on' is false reassurance (ATR–Cobb correlation is only moderate; sizeable curves can show ATR <7°), and 'refer' is noise for someone already under a surgeon. Sign: beta's sign depends on which end of the phone points to the patient's right; nothing in the protocol fixes that, so 'right side raised' is unreliable unless the helper is told the orientation. Gamma rejection: in forward bend the back surface slopes along the spine (more so at the thoracic apex and in shallow bends), so 'phone not flat' will reject legitimate readings and bias accepted readings toward horizontal segments — a real scoliometer is insensitive to that slope. Four fixed anatomical landmarks chosen by a lay helper will miss the apex; standard practice is to slide the device along the spine and record the maximum, or place it at the apex known from the X-ray. 'Peak' hides the second curve in an S pattern (opposite sign, often meaningful for the lumbar component). Measurement error: helper-measured ATR has inter-observer error of several degrees, so the 'track it' copy implies trend sensitivity the tool doesn't have until the per-user MDC is established.
findings.correction: Fork the interpretation on diagnosis status: for users with a known diagnosis, show no bands — show the reading, the same-level baseline, and 'change is not meaningful until your personal repeatability is known' (reuse the MDC machinery; expect an MDC around 3–4°). Keep 5°/7° bands only for the undiagnosed school-screening flow and add 'this does not exclude scoliosis'. Fix sign by instructing 'top of phone toward the patient's RIGHT' in the helper UI and storing orientation, or drop the side label entirely. Replace the gamma rejection with a relative check (gamma stable within the window) rather than an absolute 8° from horizontal. Add an optional 'slide slowly from neck to pelvis and we'll take the maximum' mode, and when an X-ray apex is known, add that level as the primary measurement site. Report per-level values (thoracic and lumbar separately), not just the peak. Cite Bunnell and the HK programme in the UI provenance exactly as the code comments do.
findings.evidence: Bunnell WP, Spine 1993, proposed 7° as referral cut-off after 5° over-referred (from memory). Hong Kong school screening: ATR ≥15° direct radiograph, 5–14° combined with moiré — Luk et al. Spine 2010 (from memory; the '5° carry-forward' is roughly right). Scoliometer reliability: Amendt et al. Phys Ther 1990; Côté et al. Spine 1998 on limited validity vs Cobb — UNVERIFIED specifics. Device-orientation physics (beta about x, gamma about y) verified against the code comments.

findings.area: lib/agents/cascade.ts CASCADE_MODELS + progression copy (app/session/page.tsx 'see what shifted', rapid_progression, cascade stage descriptions)
findings.claim_in_product: 'Propagation chains' per pattern: double_RT_LL: lumbar_curve_drift (lower-thoracic segment shift >12 mm) -> pelvic_rotation (>8 mm) -> hip_flexor_asymmetry -> knee_tracking_drift; right_thoracic: thoracic_curve_drift -> shoulder_asymmetry (>12 mm) -> scapular_winging -> forward_head (>18 mm). Stage 'activates' at baseline+2σ or fixed mm; description text says 'primary curve activating'. Session page: 'Same scan as before. We'll compare so you can see what shifted.' inferStiffHipFlexorSide: ≥3/4 segments shifted left -> stiff RIGHT hip flexor.
findings.problem: Plainly: these chains are invented. There is no published model, in AIS or adult deformity, in which lumbar curve change causes pelvic rotation which causes iliopsoas asymmetry which causes knee valgus in a lunge, nor one in which thoracic curve change propagates to scapular winging and then forward head. They read as a founder's personal kinesiology narrative formalised into code. Worse, the input signals are webcam mm values the team has itself declared setup-dominated (±20% torso length, yaw-confounded), so 'stage activation' is mostly camera-placement noise, and the stage labels ('lumbar_curve_drift', 'primary curve activating') tell the patient their CURVE is progressing — a claim only serial radiographs can make. Likewise 'see what shifted' implies the posture scan detects change. The hip-flexor inference rule (global trunk shift -> contralateral iliopsoas) has no anatomical basis I recognise; PSSE schools that cue the psoas do it by lumbar concavity, not by a 3-of-4 mirror count. A surgeon reading 'lumbar curve drift detected' in a handoff PDF will stop trusting the product.
findings.correction: Remove the causal chains or demote them to a plainly labelled 'things your physio may watch' checklist with no ordering, no 'activation', and no curve-drift language. Never use the words drift, progression, activating, or curve change for any signal other than a radiologist-measured Cobb angle or a repeatability-gated ATR trend, and say so in copy: 'Only an X-ray measures whether your curve has changed.' Rewrite 'see what shifted' to 'same setup so the photos are comparable'. Drop inferStiffHipFlexorSide; let the physio state the stiff side or use the patient's own stretch report. If the team wants an evidence-backed 'watch list', the only defensible items are: Cobb (radiograph), ATR at the apex (per-user MDC), Risser/maturity in adolescents, pain and PSFS.
findings.evidence: Absence of evidence: no SOSORT, SRS, or PSSE literature describes such propagation chains; the team's own pose/README conclusion that the scan cannot measure Cobb or progression. Clinical reasoning otherwise.

findings.area: lib/exercises/contraindications.ts (ABSOLUTE/RELATIVE/ASK rules and rationale strings) + exerciseContraindicated() no-op
findings.claim_in_product: ABSOLUTE for every scoliosis user: full backbends ('extreme load on the convex side'), deadlift/RDL without sign-off ('amplify rotational forces'), loaded forward flexion ('compress the spine in flexion, bad for asymmetric loading'), long end-range twists ('pull spine into existing rotation'), inversions ('stack asymmetric loads unpredictably'), side plank on the non-cued side ('reinforces the curve'). exerciseContraindicated() excludes only ABSOLUTE rules matched by libraryId, and no library item carries one, so it never excludes anything.
findings.problem: The tiering is exercise-name-based when real contraindication is condition-based, and the rationales are not physiology. There is no evidence that backbends load 'the convex side', that deadlifts amplify vertebral rotation, that inversions are unsafe in idiopathic scoliosis, or that a side plank on the other side 'reinforces the curve' — SOSORT does not restrict sport or resistance training in idiopathic scoliosis, and many adolescent patients are advised to keep lifting and playing. Telling patients their spine is fragile in these specific ways manufactures fear-avoidance, which is a documented driver of chronic pain disability. The genuinely important contraindications are missing because they depend on the patient, not the exercise: loaded/end-range flexion with osteoporosis or a recent vertebral fracture; end-range motion at junctional levels after fusion; sustained extension with symptomatic stenosis; supine work late in pregnancy; end-range rotation toward the direction of existing rotation only (a de-rotational twist is a Schroth staple, so 'twists' as a class cannot be absolute). Finally the selection-side function is dead code, so the team may believe a safety gate exists that does not.
findings.correction: Rebuild the engine as (exercise feature) x (patient condition): features = loaded flexion, end-range extension, end-range rotation (with direction), inversion, sustained asymmetric hold, impact; conditions = osteoporosis/fragility fracture, prior fusion, stenosis/radiculopathy, pregnancy, acute pain ≥7/10, adolescent in brace (brace-off time). Rules then read 'loaded flexion + osteoporosis = avoid', 'rotation toward convexity-side rotation + any = deprioritise; de-rotational direction = allowed'. Downgrade the current blanket ABSOLUTE list to 'discuss with your physio' with honest wording ('no strong evidence either way for scoliosis; your physio decides'), and remove the 'extreme load on the convex side' style explanations. Either give library items real libraryId matches and a test that asserts exerciseContraindicated() actually excludes something, or delete the function so nobody relies on it.
findings.evidence: SOSORT 2016 guidelines (Negrini et al., Scoliosis Spinal Disord 2018) — sport and physical activity are recommended, not restricted, in idiopathic scoliosis (from memory; UNVERIFIED exact wording). Fear-avoidance model of chronic pain (Vlaeyen & Linton) — general, UNVERIFIED citation detail. Osteoporotic flexion-loading fracture risk — Sinaki et al., Mayo Clin Proc 1984 (from memory). Schroth de-rotational rotation is a core PSSE element — Lehnert-Schroth.

findings.area: lib/exercises/profile.ts pattern keys; onboarding 'Four-segment shift profile'; severity labels
findings.claim_in_product: Pattern keys: right/left thoracic, right/left lumbar, 'thoracolumbar' (no side), two double patterns, 'any'. No sagittal-plane field. Four-segment lateral shift self-reported from a mirror/photo with left/right/centered chips. Severity chips: Mild (<25°), Moderate (25–40°), Severe (>40°).
findings.problem: (1) Thoracolumbar is the commonest adult (degenerative) pattern and a common AIS pattern, yet it has no convexity key, so every thoracolumbar user is silently downgraded to 'any' and receives no corrective cues at all — safe by accident, but useless, and a clinician will spot it immediately. (2) No sagittal plane: AIS is typically a lordoscoliosis (thoracic hypokyphosis); an apex HYPERkyphosis is a red flag for non-idiopathic aetiology (see red-flag finding), and in adults sagittal malalignment (flatback, positive sagittal balance) predicts symptoms better than Cobb — so 'wall stand' and 'cat-cow' cues cannot be biased correctly and the product cannot recognise the atypical case. (3) Segment shifts: a layperson estimating lateral shift of four trunk segments from a plumb line has no established reliability; rear photos preserve laterality but front/selfie captures and some cameras mirror it, so a fraction of users will enter every segment reversed with no way to detect it; and the only downstream consumer is the invented hip-flexor rule. (4) Severity labels are Cobb-based but nothing prevents a user with no radiograph choosing one; 'Severe (over 40°)' in an immature patient is a surgical-consultation range and should not be a neutral chip. Lenke/King/Rigo are NOT needed for an exercise coach — do not add them.
findings.correction: Add right_thoracolumbar / left_thoracolumbar keys (treat as lumbar for side cues, the standard PSSE approach) and map the existing 'thoracolumbar' apex + bulge answer onto them. Add a single sagittal field from the report or physio ('flat/normal/rounded upper back'); if 'rounded' and adolescent, fire the REVIEW flag; if adult with flatback, deprioritise flexion-biased resets. Drop the four-segment self-report from onboarding (keep it only as a physio-entered field), or at minimum require a rear-view photo and show the user which side is which. Gate severity on 'from an X-ray report' vs 'my guess', and if 'Severe' + age <18 surface 'this range is usually reviewed by a spine specialist; exercise is adjunctive'.
findings.evidence: Thoracic hypokyphosis as typical AIS morphology and apical kyphosis as an atypical sign — standard texts (Lovell & Winter; Dickson). Sagittal alignment and adult outcomes — Glassman et al., Spine 2005 (from memory; UNVERIFIED detail). Cobb bands (observe <25, brace 25–40/45 in immature, surgical consideration >45–50) — SRS/SOSORT conventions.

things_done_right: Red-flag architecture: three tiers with emergency truly blocking exercise on both modes, questions phrased so 'yes' raises a flag, user-facing copy that never names a condition, and a provenance string per rule. The left-thoracic-in-adolescent REVIEW rule and its provenance text are correct and something most consumer apps miss — keep it and extend the pattern.

Concave/convex is handled correctly in schroth_rotational_breathing (right thoracic -> inhale into left ribs) and bird_dog_asymmetric_hold (right thoracic -> left arm + right leg), and profile.ts states the right convention ('concave = opposite of lean'). The engine already withholds every side-dependent exercise when convexity is unknown — that fail-safe is the right design and should be the fallback whenever sources disagree.

Side plank with the thoracic-convex side down is consistent with the only published side-plank-for-scoliosis protocol (Fishman 2014) and is internally consistent across library, contraindication check and form-check. Frog in the pond is correctly restricted to right-thoracic patterns rather than mirrored blindly.
Physio prescription is authoritative when present, and the pasted programme is flagged rather than blocked — that is the correct clinician-supervised posture.

Outcome measures are sound: PSFS MCID (2 average / 3 single activity) matches the published values; SEM = SD_diff/√2 and MDC95 = 1.96·SD_diff are the correct formulas; gating trend claims behind ≥5 test–retest pairs is exactly what a clinician would ask for. McGill side-bridge L/R ratio with a 0.05 symmetry band is a recognised convention.

The posture scan has been honestly demoted: mm values flagged as ±20% and yaw-confounded, the team's own written conclusion that it cannot measure Cobb or progression, and the copy 'not a replacement for radiographic Cobb angle measurements'. Pelvic tilt in the lunge is explicitly marked out of scope rather than faked.

ATR implementation details are careful: no-sensor never returns zero, motion and roll rejection, ≥10 samples, the message states a number and a threshold rather than a diagnosis, and the 5°/7° cut-offs are cited to real programmes (HK screening, Bunnell) rather than invented. The infrastructure for a per-user ATR MDC already exists.

X-ray prompt discipline: forces 'unclear' over guessing, forbids treatment recommendations, requires ranges rather than point Cobb values, and demands user confirmation — the instincts are right even though image-reading itself is the wrong input.
LLM safety floor: fixed template on neurological/bladder symptoms with no exercise suggestion, exercise suggestions constrained to a fixed library list, and patient name redacted from agents.
Cue cadence in form-check (compensation must persist ≥2 s, ≤1 voice cue per 5 s) and the hold timer pausing when out of position are sensible, non-nagging coaching choices.

safety_informatics.headline: The red-flag engine is well-designed as a pure function, but it is wired to a screen that runs once and never again, its "urgent" tier does nothing, its adolescent rule can never fire because age is never collected, and the LLM safety floor is stripped from the prompt before the user-facing reply is written. Population gating (post-fusion, braced, osteoporotic, pregnant, Marfan/EDS) is absent, and a single wrong left/right self-report silently converts every asymmetric cue into the product's own declared contraindication.

findings.area: lib/safety/redFlags.ts questionsFor('ongoing'); app/session/page.tsx:100-127; components/onboarding/steps/SafetyStep.tsx
findings.claim_in_product: redFlags.ts defines 7 questions with askAt 'ongoing', and session/page.tsx comments: 'Re-run the stored screen every session rather than trusting the onboarding verdict indefinitely — the ruleset changes, and so do symptoms.'
findings.problem: The ongoing question set is dead code: questionsFor('ongoing') is referenced only in scripts/check-safety.ts. The session page re-runs triage() against profile.safetyScreen, i.e. the same onboarding answers, so symptoms cannot change in either direction. (a) A user who answered 'no' to bladder/bowel change at onboarding and develops it three weeks later is never asked again; the gate is blind to the one scenario it exists for. (b) A user who answered 'yes' (e.g. saddle numbness) is blocked on every session indefinitely, with no path to record 'I was seen and cleared' except re-running the whole onboarding and changing the answer — which both trains users to flip a safety answer to get past a wall and destroys the record that the flag ever fired. (c) The Telegram flag_safety tool writes only an agent_observations row; it never touches safetyScreen, so an emergency symptom disclosed in chat leaves the exercise gate fully open. Answers are a flat Record<string, boolean> with a single profile-level safety_screened_at, so there is no per-answer timestamp and no history.
findings.correction: 1) Render the 7-item ongoing set as a forced step in the session flow (before pain_check) whenever safety_screened_at is older than a fixed interval — recommend 7 days for the 3 emergency-tier items (bladder/bowel, saddle numbness, progressive weakness; three taps) and 28 days for the rest — plus a one-tap 'anything new since last time?' gate on every session that expands into the emergency 3 if 'yes'. 2) Store answers as a timestamped append-only log (question_id, value, answered_at, source: onboarding|session|chat) and have triage() use the latest value per question. 3) An emergency 'yes' must be cleared only by an explicit 'I have been assessed by a clinician' acknowledgement with a date, recorded as its own event; never by editing the original answer. 4) Have toolFlagSafety, for categories mapping to emergency rules (numbness_or_tingling with saddle/groin words, weakness, bladder/bowel), also write the corresponding screening answer so the next session is gated. 5) Add tests: 'yes at onboarding then cleared then no at session' and 'no at onboarding, yes at session' both produce the expected gate state.
findings.evidence: Code inspection of the four files named. Clinical reasoning: cauda equina and progressive motor deficit are time-critical and typically arise after enrolment, not at it; a one-time screen has near-zero sensitivity for incident symptoms. ISO 14971 hazard: 'exercise delivered during undetected emergency-tier symptoms' — the current control (one-time onboarding screen) does not mitigate the identified sequence of events.

findings.area: lib/safety/redFlags.ts triage() reducesSession; lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts; components/safety/RedFlagNotice.tsx
findings.claim_in_product: TriageResult.reducesSession = (severity === 'urgent'); check-safety.ts asserts 'unremitting night pain is urgent — reduces but does not block'. The significant_trauma rule's action text says 'Hold off on today's session.'
findings.problem: reducesSession is computed and asserted in a test, but no runtime code reads it. selectProgram() checks only blocksSession; tier bias, exercise count, hold durations and loaded items are identical for an urgent-flagged user and a clean one. So a user reporting post-fall back pain sees a banner saying 'Hold off on today's session' immediately above a full 3-5 exercise programme with a 'Begin first exercise' button — copy and behaviour contradict each other, which is exactly the kind of thing a clinician reviewer will screenshot. The cancer_history question (onboarding only, 'Have you ever been treated for cancer?') has no 'new or changed back pain' conjunct despite the rule being titled that way, so anyone with remote cancer history sees an urgent banner on every session forever; because urgent does nothing, the cost is banner fatigue rather than harm, but it also means the banner is ignored on the day it matters.
findings.correction: Define 'reduce' concretely and implement it in selectProgram: (a) significant_trauma → treat as blocksSession until acknowledged as assessed (its own action text already says so); (b) night_pain_unrelieved / systemic_illness / cancer_history → restrict candidates to tier 4 and 5 (mobility, breathing), drop any item with duration_seconds >= 30 or loads_regions including the painful region, cap at 3 items, and set mode notes to say why the session is shorter; (c) suppress Coach/Companion nudges to 'bank a session' while any urgent flag is open. Fix cancer_history by splitting it into 'ever treated for cancer' (onboarding, stored as history) AND 'new or changed back pain in the last few weeks' (ongoing); fire the rule only when both are true. Add a check-safety.ts assertion that an urgent triage produces a materially smaller/gentler programme than a clean one.
findings.evidence: Code inspection: grep for reducesSession returns only redFlags.ts, types.ts and scripts/check-safety.ts. Clinical reasoning: post-traumatic back pain is a standard 'image before loading' criterion (the product's own provenance text says so). Cancer-history red flag conventionally requires the pain conjunct (e.g. the classic Deyo/ Henschke red-flag lists pair 'history of malignancy' with current back pain) — UNVERIFIED citation from memory, but the product's own rule title already encodes the conjunct.

findings.area: lib/agents/conversation.ts handleConversation(); lib/agents/tools.ts toolFlagSafety; app/api/telegram/webhook/route.ts handleFreeText
findings.claim_in_product: CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'SAFETY FLOOR — read first... If she mentions ANY of the following, do NOT suggest exercise. Call the flag_safety tool... This rule overrides everything else.'
findings.problem: Four failure modes, all verifiable in code. (1) No deterministic pre-filter: handleFreeText passes raw text straight to handleConversation; the only thing standing between 'I can't feel my groin and I wet myself' and a suggested cat-cow is a 70B model at temperature 0.5 honouring a prompt. If it does not call flag_safety, first.content is returned to the user unfiltered ('No tool calls — direct reply'). (2) Even when the model does call flag_safety, the second pass (lines 239-252) rebuilds messages with a voice-only system prompt — the SAFETY FLOOR text is gone — and asks the model to 'compose the final user-facing reply' whose mandated shape is 'one tiny ask + reply when done'. The tool result string 'exercise suggestions paused this turn' is the only remaining hint. This is a design that invites the model to append 'try a gentle cat-cow, reply when done' after a safety flag. (3) The chat trigger list omits bladder/bowel change and saddle anaesthesia entirely, and the fixed template routes everything to 'message your physio if you can' — for a cauda equina cluster the correct instruction is emergency department today, which redFlags.ts already knows. The chat path and the screening path disagree on the same symptom. (4) flag_safety writes an observation for the next physio visit and nothing else: no Telegram escalation copy, no session gate, no notification to a supervising clinician.
findings.correction: 1) Add a deterministic pre-classifier in handleFreeText before any LLM call: a keyword/regex list in English, Traditional Chinese and common romanised Cantonese for the emergency cluster (bladder, bowel, wee/pee/poo, 尿, 大便, 失禁, can't feel, numb + groin/inner thigh/saddle/between legs, leg giving way, foot drop, 冇力) and the urgent cluster (shooting/radiating/down my leg, night pain, fever, 發燒). On an emergency hit: skip the model entirely, send the fixed redFlags.ts cauda_equina/progressive_neuro action text ('go to an emergency department now'), write the screening answer (see finding 1), and log. On an urgent hit: pass to the model but hard-strip suggest_exercise from TOOL_DEFS for that turn and post-filter the reply. 2) Post-filter every reply deterministically: if any safety category fired this turn (pre-filter or flag_safety), reject a reply that contains an exercise_pool name or any micro-movement keyword (cat-cow, figure-4, chin tuck, wall stand, walk, roller) and replace it with the template. 3) Keep the SAFETY FLOOR paragraph in the second-pass system prompt. 4) Treat the LLM's recognition as defence-in-depth, never the primary control, and document that in the hazard analysis.
findings.evidence: Code inspection of conversation.ts lines 187-267 and tools.ts 423-442. Clinical: urinary retention/incontinence and saddle anaesthesia are the core cauda equina features and require same-day emergency assessment (consistent with the product's own rule text). SaMD practice: probabilistic components must sit behind deterministic guards for hazards rated severe (IEC 62304/ISO 14971 risk-control hierarchy: inherent safety by design over information for safety).
