findings.claim_in_product: redFlags.ts: 'Left thoracic curve in an adolescent... Derived rather than asked, because the user already gave us the curve pattern at onboarding.' types.ts: 'Age in years. Only consumer today is the red-flag screen.' Roadmap targets the HK school-screening adolescent cohort.
findings.problem: No onboarding step writes ageYears. initialState sets it null, no component calls update({ ageYears }), and profile/save persists null. Consequently: (a) the atypical_curve_pattern rule — the only scoliosis-specific red flag in the set, and the one that gates MRI consideration in adolescents — is unreachable in production; it passes only in check-safety.ts where age is injected. (b) There is no age gate of any kind: a 13-year-old can complete onboarding, receive a Schroth-adjacent programme, be scanned on webcam, and be messaged at 8am by a Telegram 'companion' persona, with no guardian involvement and no clinician relationship. (c) No skeletal-maturity capture (Risser, menarche, growth velocity), so 'curve first appeared after you'd finished growing' is asked of users who cannot know whether they have. The product's own docs/product-strategy.html already identifies telling a growing adolescent their curve is stable as a specific danger; the code has no way to know who is growing.
findings.correction: 1) Collect date of birth (not age) as a required field on the welcome step; derive ageYears at runtime. 2) Hard gate: age < 18 → the self-guided path is disabled; the product requires (i) a guardian consent record with contact details, (ii) a named supervising clinician or a pasted physio programme, and (iii) the adolescent's own assent text in age-appropriate language. Until all three exist, show only the ATR self-check and the handoff PDF, not exercises. 3) For minors, disable free-text LLM chat and proactive Companion nudges by default (safeguarding: an adult-voiced persona texting a 14-year-old unsupervised will not pass an ethics board), disable posture-scan mm/asymmetry numbers (body-image harm), and never display 'stable'/'improving' language on any scan-derived trend. 4) Capture menarche status/Risser if known from the X-ray report, and re-word adult_onset to be asked only when age >= 18. 5) For an REB submission expect to need: parental consent + child assent forms in Traditional Chinese and English, a data-minimisation statement for minors, an adverse-event and escalation pathway naming a clinician, a plan for the false-reassurance hazard, and a statement that the school-screening cohort is not recruited via the school without the Department of Health's involvement.
findings.evidence: Code inspection (grep of ageYears across components/ and app/). Left thoracic curves in adolescents warranting MRI consideration is standard teaching, consistent with the product's own provenance text. Consent: in Hong Kong, medical consent for under-18s is ordinarily obtained from a parent/guardian unless the minor is assessed as competent (Gillick-style reasoning is applied in HK practice) — UNVERIFIED from memory; PDPO has no statutory digital age of consent but the PCPD publishes children's-data guidance — UNVERIFIED from memory.

findings.area: lib/exercises/contraindications.ts; lib/exercises/library.ts; lib/outcomes/compute.ts; onboarding intake
findings.claim_in_product: 'loaded_forward_flexion' and 'long_static_twists' are ABSOLUTE for every user; 'long_static_asymmetric_holds' >60s is RELATIVE. Library prescribes side plank 3x30s, bird-dog asymmetric holds, supine hip bridge, frog-in-the-pond (supine), schroth rotational breathing. Outcomes include Sorensen hold and side-bridge endurance to failure. No intake question about surgery, brace, bone density, pregnancy, connective-tissue disorder.
findings.problem: The contraindication set is calibrated to one phenotype (adult, unfused, idiopathic, no comorbidity) and applied to everyone. Concrete gaps: (1) Post-fusion: a fused adult can enter as 'unknown' curve and receive rotational breathing and pelvic de-rotation aimed at segments that are now rigid, plus lateral flexion (sitting_waist_fold) and 30s side planks at the junction above/below the fusion. Standard post-PSF advice restricts bending, lifting and twisting for roughly 6 months and end-range twisting over the fused segment indefinitely; the app has no field to know surgery happened. (2) Braced adolescents: no capture of brace wear, so no guidance on in-brace vs out-of-brace exercise or protecting wear hours. (3) Adults >60 / degenerative curves: possible osteoporosis — here loaded and end-range flexion IS a well-evidenced hazard, yet the product cannot distinguish this user from a 25-year-old, and the physio-cleared path only flags, never blocks. (4) Pregnancy: supine work (hip bridge, single-leg bridge, frog-in-the-pond) after mid-pregnancy and ligamentous laxity are not handled. (5) Marfan and related aortopathies: every isometric hold in the library (side plank 30s, bird-dog holds, wall stand 60s) and both endurance-to-failure outcome tests (Sorensen, side-bridge) involve sustained isometric effort and breath-holding, which aortopathy guidance advises avoiding. (6) Hypermobility/EDS: end-range stretching cues ('reach to lengthen', 'fold') and shoulder-loaded side plank need modification. Meanwhile the ABSOLUTE ban on 'loaded forward flexion' for a healthy 25-year-old with a 20-degree curve is stronger than the evidence supports and will be read by physios as over-cautious, which erodes trust in the flags that matter.
findings.correction: Add a 6-item intake block (all yes/no, asked before the safety screen): spinal surgery (with year and levels if known), currently wearing a brace (hours/day), diagnosed osteoporosis/osteopenia or age >= 60, currently pregnant or <12 weeks postpartum, diagnosed connective-tissue disorder (Marfan, EDS, Loeys-Dietz), known heart/aorta condition. Map each to a population profile that (a) forces physio_cleared mode (self-guided disabled) and (b) adds deterministic library exclusions by libraryId — the exerciseContraindicated() hook already exists but has no libraryId entries; populate it: fusion → exclude schroth_rotational_breathing, frog_in_the_pond, sitting_waist_fold, side_plank, any 'de-rotation' cue; osteoporosis → exclude forward-flexion items and cap flexion cues, keep the existing flexion rule as ABSOLUTE for this group and downgrade it to ask_physio for AIS; pregnancy → exclude supine items after 20 weeks and flag prone/side-plank; aortopathy → exclude all timed isometric holds >10s and both endurance outcome tests, replace with rep-based work; EDS → strip 'reach/lengthen/fold' end-range cues. Show the physio handoff PDF with the population profile stated prominently.
findings.evidence: Post-PSF activity restriction of ~6 months for bending/lifting/twisting and staged return to sport is common surgeon guidance (survey literature, e.g. Rubery & Bradford 2002 — UNVERIFIED from memory). Osteoporosis: Sinaki & Mikkelsen 1984 reported markedly higher vertebral fracture incidence with flexion exercise than extension in osteoporotic women — UNVERIFIED from memory but a widely taught result. Marfan: AHA/ACC thoracic aortic disease guidance advises avoiding isometric exercise, heavy lifting and Valsalva — UNVERIFIED from memory. Pregnancy: ACOG exercise guidance advises caution with prolonged supine positioning later in pregnancy — UNVERIFIED from memory. Code inspection confirms the exclusion hook exists and is empty.

findings.area: components/onboarding/steps/CurveStep.tsx primaryLeanSide; lib/exercises/profile.ts deriveRegionalSides; lib/atr/compute.ts rotationSide(); components/onboarding/steps/XrayStep.tsx; lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts sidesUnknown
findings.claim_in_product: selectProgram.ts: 'A coin flip is not an acceptable default when the downside is making someone's scoliosis worse' — so unknown convexity withholds side-dependent exercises. checkSidePlankSide: holding the wrong side 'reinforces the curve' and is ABSOLUTE.
findings.problem: The withholding logic is correct but protects only against 'unknown', not against 'wrong'. A single flipped left/right answer to 'which way does your back bulge' inverts thoracicConvex and lumbarConvex, and every downstream cue flips with it: side plank goes to the side the product itself labels an absolute contraindication, bird-dog long hold goes to the wrong pattern, hip-bridge press-down goes to the wrong pelvis, waist fold and child's-pose reach go the wrong way, and the form-check coaches the user to hold the wrong side longer. There is no second signal, yet two are already in the product: (a) ATR rotationSide() returns 'right' when the right side is raised (rotation convention of a right-convex thoracic curve) and is never compared with primaryLeanSide; (b) the Gemini-parsed X-ray convex_side is applied to the profile but never reconciled with the user's manual answer if both exist. Left/right confusion is not a rare edge case: the mirror asked for in the segment-shift step preserves the user's own left/right, but a photo taken from the front, a mirrored selfie, or a partner describing 'your right' from in front of you all flip it; a standard PA radiograph is displayed as if facing the patient, so a layperson reading their own film off a phone will report the convex side flipped roughly half the time.
findings.correction: 1) Treat convexity as a claim needing corroboration: store the source of each side (self_report | xray_report | atr | clinician) with a confidence. 2) Cross-check at every point where a second source exists: if peak ATR magnitude >= 5 degrees and rotationSide() at the main_thoracic level disagrees with thoracicConvex, or the X-ray report's convex_side disagrees with the manual answer, set thoracicConvex to null (falling back to the existing withholding path) and show a plain-language reconciliation screen ('your phone reading and your answer point in different directions — which is right? Ask your physio if unsure'). 3) In CurveStep, replace the abstract question with a disambiguation task: show two mirrored back-view silhouettes and ask the user to pick the one that looks like their back from behind, with explicit copy 'this is as if someone is standing behind you'. 4) In physio_cleared mode, prefer the physio programme's side words over the profile when they conflict, and flag the conflict on the handoff PDF. 5) Fix the library's internal inconsistency first (sitting_waist_fold says right_thoracic concave is RIGHT; schroth_rotational_breathing says LEFT) — the cross-check is meaningless while the library disagrees with itself about which side is concave. 6) Add a test: profile right_thoracic + ATR peak -6 degrees at main_thoracic → sides null and a reconciliation note.
findings.evidence: Code inspection: rotationSide is defined in lib/atr/compute.ts and unused in components/. Radiograph display convention (viewer's left = patient's right on a PA/AP film) is standard radiology teaching. The side-plank convex-side-down convention the product uses matches the published side-plank-for-scoliosis protocol (Fishman et al., 2014 — UNVERIFIED from memory), which makes the wrong-side harm the product's own stated hazard rather than my assertion.

findings.area: lib/exercises/contraindications.ts namePatterns; lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts physioClearedMode
findings.claim_in_product: Absolute rules match a pasted physio programme by regex on exercise name; e.g. wheel_pose_full_backbend includes /\bbridge\s*(?:full|complete)\b/i; side plank side is read from asymmetric_cues containing 'right side' or 'left side'.
findings.problem: Concrete failures: (1) 'Full bridge 3x10' is NOT flagged — the pattern requires 'bridge' before 'full', so the exact phrase the digest lists as banned passes clean, while 'hip bridge' correctly passes. (2) /\bclean\b/i (heavy_compound_lifts) fires on 'keep a clean neutral spine' or 'clean up the lunge form' — a physio's cue text becomes an ask-physio flag on their own programme. (3) /\broll[\s-]?up/i fires on 'foam roll upper back' and 'roll up the mat after' (the pattern has no trailing boundary), flagging a foam-roller release as ABSOLUTE loaded forward flexion. (4) /\binversion\b/i fires on 'ankle inversion/eversion' rehab. (5) /twist.*(?:hold|held)/i fires on 'gentle supine twist, hold 5 breaths' — the very kind of low-load mobility a physio might legitimately prescribe — with ABSOLUTE severity, but misses 'seated rotation, 60s each side' which has no 'twist' token. (6) Matching runs on pex.name, an LLM-normalised field, not on source_text, so the model's paraphrase decides whether a rule fires. (7) Side-plank side detection needs the literal 'right side'/'left side'; 'R side', 'lie on your right', 'right elbow down', or a Chinese cue ('右邊向下') all yield null and the wrong-side check silently passes. Because the physio path never blocks, false positives here cost clinician trust rather than safety, but false negatives (1, 5, 7) remove the only automated check on the path the product treats as authoritative.
findings.correction: 1) Fix the reversed pattern: /\b(?:full|complete)\s*bridge\b/i and /\bbridge\s*(?:full|complete)\b/i both. 2) Add trailing boundaries and exclusions: /\broll[\s-]?ups?\b/i with a negative lookbehind for 'foam'; drop the bare /\bclean\b/ in favour of /\b(?:power|hang|squat)?\s*cleans?\b(?!\s*(?:up|line|form|neutral))/i or require a load token (kg, lb, barbell); scope 'inversion' to /\b(?:yoga\s*)?inversions?\b(?!.*(?:ankle|foot))/i. 3) Run patterns against both name and source_text, and record which field matched. 4) Have the parse-program LLM emit a structured 'side' enum (left|right|both|null) and a 'load' enum (bodyweight|light|heavy|null) per exercise, then match rules on those fields rather than free text; keep regex as a fallback only. 5) Distinguish rule severity by load and duration where the rule depends on them (long_static_twists should require a hold >= 30s or 'end-range' token to be ABSOLUTE; otherwise ask_physio). 6) Add a regression fixture of 30 real physio-programme strings (English + Chinese + shorthand) with expected hits, and run it in check-safety.ts.
findings.evidence: Direct regex evaluation against the patterns in contraindications.ts. No external source needed.

findings.area: lib/safety/redFlags.ts SCREENING_QUESTIONS; components/onboarding/steps/SafetyStep.tsx
findings.claim_in_product: Nine yes/no questions phrased so 'yes' always raises a flag; every question must be answered; 'Most people answer no to all of these.'
findings.problem: False-negative modes, per question: bladder_bowel_change — help text lists urgency and loss of awareness but omits retention ('can't pee / can't fully empty'), which is the cardinal cauda equina feature; a user in retention who has not leaked answers 'no'. saddle_numbness — 'sit-bones' is an anatomy-class idiom a 14-year-old or a Cantonese-first speaker will not know; 'pins and needles' is likewise idiomatic; no plain 'between your legs / around your bottom / genitals' wording. leg_weakness_progressing — 'getting worse recently' misses new-but-stable foot drop and undefined 'recently'; a user with a leg that gives way weekly but 'not worse' answers 'no'. night_pain — a two-clause conjunction ('wakes you AND stays when you change position') forced into one yes/no; users who are woken but do move around answer 'no' when the clinically relevant half is true. fever_or_weight_loss — 'account for' is idiomatic; also a disjunction, so a 'yes' cannot be attributed. adult_onset — asked of everyone including minors and people who do not know their skeletal maturity. There is no 'not sure' option, so uncertainty is forced into 'no'. The whole instrument is English-only for a product whose second cohort is Hong Kong school-screening adolescents. The framing line 'Most people answer no to all of these' is a social-desirability nudge toward 'no' immediately above the emergency items. False-positive costs are modest (an urgent banner that does nothing; an emergency block that can be honestly cleared once finding 1 is fixed), so the instrument should be tuned toward sensitivity.
findings.correction: 1) Rewrite each item in plain language at roughly a 10-year-old reading level and provide Traditional Chinese: e.g. 'In the last few days, have you had trouble peeing, not been able to feel when you need to go, or leaked wee or poo?'; 'Is there any numb or tingly feeling around your bottom, between your legs, or on the inside of your thighs?'; 'Has a leg felt weak, given way, or has your foot caught or dragged when you walk — even if it is not getting worse?' 2) Split every conjunction/disjunction into separate items (night pain wakes you? / does it settle when you move?; fever? / weight loss?). 3) Add a third answer, 'Not sure', which triage() treats as 'yes' for emergency-tier items and as 'flag for review' for others; never as 'no'. 4) Remove the 'Most people answer no' line or move it below the emergency items. 5) Gate adult_onset on age >= 18 (needs finding 4). 6) Have a clinician and a plain-language reviewer sign off the wording, and record that in the design history file.
findings.evidence: Code inspection of SCREENING_QUESTIONS. Clinical: urinary retention and saddle anaesthesia are the features emphasised in cauda equina pathways (e.g. UK GIRFT/NHS cauda equina pathways — UNVERIFIED from memory). Health-literacy convention: screening items should be single-construct, avoid idiom, and offer an uncertainty option; compound items lower sensitivity (general survey-methodology principle, no specific citation).

things_done_right: Emergency gating is implemented inside the pure selectProgram() function, not in the page, and the physio-cleared path is gated too — the check-safety.ts test 'a physio-prescribed programme is gated too' is exactly the assertion an auditor wants to see. Keep this structure and extend it (urgent tier, population gates) in the same place.

Screening questions are uniformly 'yes = flag' polarity, every item must be answered explicitly, and unanswered is deliberately not treated as 'no' (SafetyStep.tsx comment and OnboardingState type). This is textbook screening-instrument hygiene; keep it when adding a 'Not sure' option.
The left-thoracic-adolescent rule is derived from the profile rather than asked — correct instinct; it only needs age to actually be collected.

User-facing copy never names a condition, and handoffSummary() explicitly states answers are self-reported and unverified. Both are the right posture for a non-diagnostic SaMD and will survive an ethics review.

Unknown convexity withholds every side-dependent exercise rather than defaulting a side, with an honest note to the user. The comment in selectProgram.ts ('a coin flip is not an acceptable default') is the right hazard reasoning; it just needs extending to 'wrong' as well as 'unknown'.

The ATR module rejects rather than corrects bad readings (roll > 8 degrees, drift > 1.5 degrees, < 10 samples, no sensor never reads as zero) and reports number-plus-threshold without a diagnosis. That is a measurement module a clinician can trust, and it is the natural corroboration signal for convexity.

The team has already demoted the webcam posture scan to qualitative-only and documented why (setup-dominated, yaw-confounded). Acknowledging a measurement's limits in code comments is rare and valuable; carry the same honesty into the cascade models, which still consume those mm values.

Agents never receive the user's name; the coach route re-derives side cues server-side from the profile rather than trusting the LLM's side words. That pattern — LLM proposes, deterministic code decides — is precisely what the chat safety floor should copy.

An existing scripted safety test suite (scripts/check-safety.ts) runs triage, gating and copy-leak checks. It is the right place to add the regressions recommended above rather than building new infrastructure.

biomech.headline: The ATR inclinometer is the right instrument and its maths is mostly sound, but its sign convention is undefined, its "roll" check measures the wrong thing, and its screening bands are meaningless for the diagnosed adults it serves; the outcome module's MDC identities are correct but gated on far too few pairs and never wired to the side-bridge trend; three of the five webcam form checks (and all surviving mm posture bands) sit at or below single-camera landmark error.

findings.area: lib/atr/compute.ts (AtrReading.deg sign, rotationSide) + app/atr/page.tsx helper instructions
findings.claim_in_product: "Positive = the user's right side is raised, which is the convention a right-convex thoracic curve produces." The results card labels each level "X° right up / left up" and summarise() reports side.
findings.problem: Beta is defined in the DEVICE frame: positive beta means the device's top edge (+y, the camera end) is higher than its bottom edge. Which of the patient's sides that corresponds to depends entirely on whether the helper laid the phone with its top pointing to the patient's right or left — and the instructions only say "flat across your back, screen up, square to your spine". A helper standing on the patient's left will naturally point the top the opposite way from one standing on the right, so the "right up / left up" label is a coin flip between sessions and between helpers. There is no sensor that can recover this (alpha is compass heading, useless indoors and unstable near flat). A flipped sign on a repeat reading would also read as a spurious 2x change in a future trend engine.
findings.correction: (1) Instruct explicitly and enforce by UI: "Point the top of the phone (camera end) toward the patient's RIGHT." Show a diagram. (2) Before saving each reading ask the helper one confirmation: "Which side of the back was the camera end pointing to?" and flip the sign accordingly; store `topPointedTo` with the reading. (3) In page.tsx, the per-level side label ignores the 1° deadband that rotationSide() applies — use rotationSide() there too so a 0.3° reading is not labelled "right up". (4) Never let ATR sign feed convexity inference until (1)–(2) exist.
findings.evidence: W3C DeviceOrientation Event spec: alpha/beta/gamma are intrinsic Z-X'-Y'' Tait–Bryan angles in the device frame; beta is rotation about the device x-axis (short axis) with positive beta lifting the +y (top) edge — hence beta=90 when held upright, which lib/pose/tilt.ts itself relies on. Mapping device-top to patient-side is a placement fact, not a sensor fact. High confidence on the axis math; the UI omission is verified in app/atr/page.tsx lines 136–139.

findings.area: lib/atr/compute.ts MAX_ROLL_DEG=8, MAX_DRIFT_DEG=1.5, SAMPLE_MS=2500, TRUNK_LEVELS hints; code comment ICC 0.94–0.99
findings.claim_in_product: "a rolled phone reads a component of its own tilt as trunk rotation" (so gamma>8° is rejected as 'phone_not_flat'); user copy: "Lay it down so both long edges touch"; header comment: smartphone apps validate at ICC 0.94–0.99 vs Bunnell, "at or above the device's own repeatability".
findings.problem: (a) The cross-talk claim is mathematically false under the W3C Z-X'-Y'' convention: the world z-component of the device long axis is sin(beta) exactly, independent of gamma, so beta IS the long-axis elevation whatever the roll. Gamma with the phone across the back is the FORE–AFT slope of the back surface at that level, i.e. a measure of bend depth/kyphosis — which is legitimately non-zero and level-dependent. Rejecting it as 'not flat' with copy about 'both long edges touching' is wrong physics and will produce repeated confusing rejections at the upper-thoracic and lumbar levels. (b) The real error sources are not roll: (i) lay-helper level selection and lateral centring — a flat phone has no spinous-process notch, so it seats on whichever two high points it finds and can sit 1–2 cm off the midline; the scoliometer's notch and rocker base enforce centring; (ii) the helper taps 'Take reading' on a phone already lying on the back — the tap tilts the phone and sampling starts at that instant, so the 1.5° range check will trip repeatedly; (iii) accelerometer zero-offset (0.5–2° on consumer phones) is never calibrated — the Bunnell protocol checks the instrument reads 0 on a level surface; (iv) 2.5 s does not span a breath cycle (~4 s), and range (max−min) is spike-sensitive. (c) The ICC 0.94–0.99 figures come from clinician-placed devices, several with a purpose-built sleeve/holder with a spinal notch, on marked levels, same day. None of that transfers to an untrained helper at home; the comment should not imply it does.
findings.correction: (1) Rename the gamma check to a bend-depth check and use it as Bunnell intended: guide the helper (who CAN see the screen) with a live bubble-level to 'ask them to bend a little more/less until this level is horizontal'; tolerance ±10° is fine because there is no cross-talk into beta. (2) Replace discrete tapped levels with a SWEEP: helper slides the phone slowly from the shoulder blades to the pelvis; sample continuously; per-sample accept if |gamma|≤10°; report the max |beta| (this is exactly what a clinician does with a scoliometer) plus the 4 level values read off by time/position markers. (3) Start sampling 1.5 s after the tap (or use a 3-2-1 voice countdown) and use a 4 s window; reject on SD>0.7° or IQR rather than range; use the median. (4) Add a zero-offset step: lay the phone on a table and store beta_offset; or two-position zeroing (read, rotate 180° in-plane, read; true = (b1−b2)/2). (5) Optionally read DeviceMotion accelerationIncludingGravity and compute atan2(g_y, g_z) as a cross-check — no gimbal problem exists near flat, so this is about cross-browser consistency, not singularities. (6) Rewrite the comment: cite the validation studies for what they are (clinician, holder, marked levels) and state that home-helper repeatability is unknown until atrPairsFrom() data exist — which is exactly why that function is there.
findings.evidence: Axis math from the W3C DeviceOrientation spec (high confidence). Bunnell WP, JBJS Am 1984 describes adjusting forward bend so the measured level is horizontal and zero-checking the scoliometer. Smartphone-vs-scoliometer validations (Franko et al. J Pediatr Orthop 2012; Izatt et al. Scoliosis 2012 with an acrylic sleeve; Balg et al. J Pediatr Orthop 2014) — all clinician-placed; the ICC values in the code and docs/product-strategy.html are consistent with what I recall from these but the exact numbers are UNVERIFIED from memory. ATR sensitivity to trunk-flexion angle and breathing: clinical convention, UNVERIFIED citation.

findings.area: lib/atr/compute.ts ATR_MONITOR_DEG=5, ATR_REFERRAL_DEG=7, summarise() peak-only, message copy
findings.claim_in_product: ">= 5° the level Hong Kong's school screening programme carries forward; >= 7° the conventional Bunnell referral threshold"; the message tells a user with a 9° peak "this is worth showing to yours" and one at 4° that they are "below the 5° mark clinicians typically follow up on".
findings.problem: (a) These are SCREENING thresholds for undiagnosed adolescents. The product's users are diagnosed scoliosis patients (adults first): nearly all will read ≥7° at the apex by definition, so the 'refer' band fires on every session and carries no information, while a 4° reading in someone with a known 30° curve is not reassurance. (b) The HK programme (as I recall it) carried ATR 5–14° forward to moiré topography and referred for radiograph only at ATR ≥15° or moiré ≥2 lines; it never used 7° — so pairing '5° HK' with '7° Bunnell' mixes two protocols. (c) Peak-across-levels is correct for screening (Bunnell records the maximum) but is the wrong summary for longitudinal use: the apex level, and the opposite-signed lumbar hump in an S-curve, are the clinically meaningful per-level facts, and peak-of-4 is also the noisiest statistic available (max of noisy values is biased upward).
findings.correction: For any user with a confirmed diagnosis: drop the within/monitor/refer banding from the message; show the per-level readings, the baseline value at each level, and the change vs baseline with a 'not yet distinguishable from noise' note until the user's own ATR MDC exists (atrPairsFrom already collects the pairs). Keep the 5°/7° screening bands only for the future HK adolescent-screening flow, and describe HK's protocol accurately (5° → further assessment; radiograph referral at higher ATR/moiré criteria — verify the exact numbers against Luk et al. 2010 / Fong et al. 2015 before shipping copy). Retain 'peak' as one summary but trend per level, and record which level was the peak.
findings.evidence: Bunnell WP, JBJS Am 1984 and Spine 1993 (7° referral criterion ≈ Cobb 20°); SRS/POSNA/AAOS/AAP 2015 position statement uses ATR 7°. HK screening protocol per Luk KDK et al., Spine 2010 and Fong DYT et al., Spine J 2015 — protocol details UNVERIFIED from memory. That screening bands are uninformative in a diagnosed cohort is clinical reasoning.

findings.area: lib/outcomes/compute.ts SIDE_BRIDGE_SYMMETRY_TOLERANCE=0.05, ratioTrend(minChange=0.08), enduranceMdc()
findings.claim_in_product: "symmetric" if weaker/stronger is within 0.05 of 1.0 (McGill convention); trend 'improving/worsening' called when the ratio moves ≥0.08; enduranceMdc() exists as the intended replacement.
findings.problem: (a) McGill's 0.05 is a TRAINING TARGET from his normative database, not a detection limit; it says nothing about how much a ratio can move on re-test. Endurance holds to failure are motivation- and day-dependent, and a ratio compounds two noisy numbers: with a plausible 10–15% CV per side, the ratio's CV is ~15–20%, so its MDC95 is on the order of 0.3–0.5, not 0.08. Concretely, 20 s vs 22 s → 0.909; 20 s vs 24 s → 0.833: two extra seconds on one side is already a 'worsening' call. (b) enduranceMdc() returns an MDC in SECONDS, never in ratio units, and nothing calls it from ratioTrend — the 'placeholder until per-user MDC' has no path to being replaced. (c) enduranceMdc() calls computeRepeatability() directly and so bypasses MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC=5 — it will happily return an MDC from 2 pairs.
findings.correction: Trend on ln(seconds) per side, not on the ratio: MDC on log-seconds is scale-free and the side-asymmetry is then ln(R)−ln(L), whose MDC is √2 × the single-side log-MDC. Wire ratioTrend (or its replacement) to that per-user MDC; until ≥10 pairs exist, use a conservative default of ~20% change (ratio ±0.2) and label it an estimate. Keep 0.05 only as McGill's target band in the UI copy ('the training target is within 5%'), never as a change detector. Route enduranceMdc through buildMdcTable so the minimum-pairs gate applies. Record and display which side changed, since 'ratio rose' hides whether the weak side improved or the strong side declined.
findings.evidence: McGill SM, Childs A, Liebenson C. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 1999;80:941–944 (normative endurance times); the RSB/LSB '≤0.05 from 1.0' guideline is from McGill's Low Back Disorders text (UNVERIFIED page). McGill 1999 reported very high 5-day reliability in young healthy subjects; later work in athletes/patients (e.g. Evans, Refshauge, Adams, J Sci Med Sport 2007) found lower ICCs and large SEMs — UNVERIFIED numbers. Error propagation for a ratio is standard: CV(R/L) ≈ √(CV_R² + CV_L²). Code facts verified.

findings.area: lib/outcomes/compute.ts EnduranceTest side_bridge_left/right vs lib/exercises/contraindications.ts (side plank wrong side; asymmetric hold >60 s relative) and library side_plank_convex_thoracic_side_down
findings.claim_in_product: The outcome module asks users to hold a side bridge to failure on BOTH sides monthly. The contraindication engine says side plank must be done convex-thoracic-side DOWN, "holding the other side reinforces the curve", flags any asymmetric static hold >60 s as relative, and the library says "wrong side held long is a contraindication".
findings.problem: The product's headline outcome measure requires exactly the movement the product's own safety rule calls a contraindication: a maximal-duration side plank with the convex side UP, by definition an asymmetric hold that will exceed 60 s in most adults. A clinician reading both modules will ask which one the team believes. The underlying rule is itself weakly evidenced (a single uncontrolled serial-case series), so the inconsistency is not resolvable by simply banning the test.
findings.correction: Pick one coherent position and encode it in both modules. Recommended: (1) keep the bilateral side-bridge TEST (a ratio needs both sides) but cap the test at 60–90 s per side and record time-to-form-break rather than time-to-exhaustion; (2) restate the side-plank rule as a TRAINING-dose rule ('daily prolonged holds are prescribed convex-side down; a capped bilateral test is fine') and downgrade 'wrong side' from absolute-contextual to relative with an honest evidence note; (3) have the contraindication regex explicitly exempt the outcome-test session so physio_cleared mode doesn't flag the test itself.
findings.evidence: Fishman LM, Groessl EJ, Sherman KJ, Global Adv Health Med 2014 — uncontrolled serial case series of convex-side-down side plank in scoliosis; it is the only source I know for the side-selection rule (UNVERIFIED details). The contradiction itself is verified in the two source files.

findings.area: lib/pose/repeatability.ts MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC=5, computeRepeatability(); used by atrPairsFrom and enduranceMdc
findings.claim_in_product: SEM = SD_diff/√2; MDC95 = 1.96·SD_diff; LoA = bias ± 1.96·SD_diff; "needs ≥5 pairs"; posture/endurance trends gated on the resulting MDC.
findings.problem: The identities are correct. The gate is not. With 5 pairs (4 df) the 95% CI on the SD spans roughly 0.60× to 2.9× the point estimate (chi-square: √(4/11.14) to √(4/0.484)), so the MDC can be under-estimated by ~40% or over-estimated ~3-fold — i.e. the gate will call noise 'real change' or hide real change, with a confident-sounding one-decimal number attached. Even 10 pairs gives ~0.69×–1.83×. Further: (a) the bias term is computed but never tested — a significant bias (fatigue, learning) means the pairs are not exchangeable and SD_diff/√2 understates SEM; (b) endurance holds are heteroscedastic (error scales with duration) so a raw-seconds MDC is wrong at both ends; (c) no ICC is computed, which is what any reviewer for Spine or Gait & Posture would ask for first, alongside a Bland–Altman plot with the LoA you already compute.
findings.correction: (1) Raise the per-user gate to 10 pairs and, below ~20, multiply by the upper 95% confidence bound of SD_diff (s·√((n−1)/χ²_{0.025,n−1})) so the MDC errs conservative; expose n on the UI line. (2) Pool a population MDC across consenting users (ICC(2,1) with 95% CI, SEM, MDC95, Bland–Altman with proportional-bias check) and use it as the prior, shrinking toward the personal estimate as pairs accumulate. (3) Log-transform endurance seconds before computing repeatability. (4) Test bias with a paired t-test (or require |bias| < SEM) and, if it fails, tell the user the protocol drifted rather than emitting an MDC. (5) Add an ICC(2,1) to the Repeatability type — it costs ten lines.
findings.evidence: Standard test–retest definitions: SEM = SD_diff/√2 (when derived from paired differences), MDC95 = 1.96·√2·SEM (Weir JP, J Strength Cond Res 2005; de Vet et al., Measurement in Medicine, 2011). Chi-square CI on a variance is textbook. COSMIN recommends ≥50 participants for a reliability study — the per-user context is different, but the small-n interval width is not negotiable. High confidence on the statistics.

findings.area: lib/exercises/formCheck/{birdDog,hipBridge,lunge,tStretch}.ts thresholds (0.018, 0.012, 0.025, 0.018, SPINE_ROTATION_RATIO=0.25) and lib/pose/thresholds.ts BANDS (5/15 mm), still consumed by PoseScanner.tsx and StickerOverlay.tsx
findings.claim_in_product: Bird dog: hip drop if L/R hip y differs by >0.018 (major cue), spine rotation if shoulder-line vs hip-line angle differs >0.25; hip bridge: uneven lift >0.012 and a personalised MAJOR 'press your X hip down' cue; T-stretch hip rotation >0.018; lunge hip drop >0.025. Posture scan still classifies shoulder/hip/segment mm into within ≤5 / monitor ≤15 / significant.
findings.problem: Physical meaning: 0.018 of frame height at a typical 1.5–2.5 m webcam distance (vertical FOV ~45° → 1.2–2.1 m of scene) is ~2–4 cm; 0.012 is ~1.5–2.5 cm. MediaPipe hip landmarks are among its noisiest (clothing, no bony feature) and in the views these exercises are performed in — side or three-quarter view of a horizontal body — the FAR hip is occluded and inferred, so L/R hip y-difference is dominated by (i) perspective (the near hip is always lower in the image → a systematic, not random, 'lift your near hip' cue every session), (ii) MediaPipe left/right swaps in profile views, and (iii) inference noise comparable to the threshold itself. The 2 s persistence filter removes random jitter but not these biases. birdDog's 'ratio' is actually an unwrapped atan2 angle difference in radians (0.25 rad ≈ 14°): in a side view both landmark pairs nearly coincide so the angles are random, and there is no ±π wrap — shoulderAngle 3.1 vs hipAngle −3.1 reads as 6.2 rad of 'twist'. Triage from one camera: PLAUSIBLE — side plank sag/pike/head (three collinear landmarks, ~5–8 cm deviation, in the image plane), rep counting for hip bridge and lunge, T-stretch back-knee angle (2D projection in a side view); THEATRE — bird-dog hip drop and spine rotation, hip-bridge L/R uneven-lift and the personalised press-down cue, T-stretch hip rotation, lunge knee-collapse under camera yaw. The surviving 5/15 mm posture bands are narrower than the module's own stated ±20% torso-length scale error and ~9 mm-per-2°-yaw confound, so they classify noise.
findings.correction: (1) Remove or demote to 'minor' every L/R hip-height cue (birdDog hip_drop, hipBridge press_down_side_high/uneven_hips, tStretch hip_rotated) until validated against a second view or a marker; never emit a side-specific pelvic cue at 'major' severity from inferred landmarks. (2) Delete birdDog spine_rotation or fix it: wrap the angle difference to [−π, π], require both shoulders and both hips visibility >0.7 and a shoulder-width/torso-length ratio proving a rear or front view. (3) Express every threshold in body-relative units (fraction of hip width or shoulder–hip length, as birdDog already does for displacement) rather than frame fraction, and set each at ≥3× the per-session landmark SD you already estimate during the baseline-stability phase (BASELINE_MOVEMENT_TOLERANCE). (4) Require and verify camera placement per exercise (rear/front at hip height for any pelvic check). (5) Remove the mm BANDS from PoseScanner/StickerOverlay; if any band survives, express it in degrees of tilt and gate it on a measured MDC — otherwise show the number with 'no change detectable'.
findings.evidence: MediaPipe Pose outputs image-normalised coordinates; hip landmark error and profile-view L/R confusion are well known from Vicon/OpenCap comparison studies (image-plane joint-centre errors of a few cm are typical) — magnitudes UNVERIFIED from memory. Geometry (FOV → cm per normalised unit) is arithmetic. The atan2 wrap bug and the live use of BANDS are verified in source (birdDog.ts lines 268–274; PoseScanner.tsx lines 678–759; StickerOverlay.tsx lines 69–126). The team's own ±20% / yaw statements are in the digest.

findings.area: lib/outcomes/compute.ts psfsAverage(), psfsChange(), PSFS_MCID_AVERAGE=2, PSFS_MCID_SINGLE=3
findings.claim_in_product: "Published MCID is around 2 points on the average score and 3 points on a single activity." psfsAverage() averages whatever activities are present in each entry; perActivity pairs by label string.
findings.problem: The values match the conventional Stratford figures and are defensible, but (a) the 3-point single-activity figure is usually reported as an MDC (detectable change), not an MCID, and MCID estimates for the average score vary by condition (values in the ~1.3–2 range appear for low back pain and other regions), with no PSFS validation in scoliosis at all; (b) psfsChange() computes from/to averages over different activity sets — if the patient adds an activity at follow-up, or renames one, the average shifts without any change in function. PSFS scoring convention is to average only activities rated at both time points; (c) matching by free-text label breaks on any edit.
findings.correction: Compute the average change over the intersection of activity ids (not labels) present at both time points; block adding activities mid-episode or start a new episode when they change. Relabel constants PSFS_MDC_SINGLE=3 and PSFS_MCID_AVERAGE=2 with a comment that both are borrowed from non-scoliosis populations and that 2 points is on the conservative end of published MCIDs. Consider also reporting the MDC90 for the average score.
findings.evidence: Stratford P, Gill C, Westaway M, Binkley J. Physiother Can 1995 (original PSFS; MDC ≈2 average, ≈3 single activity); Horn KK et al. JOSPT 2012 systematic review (MCID varies by region); Maughan & Lewis Eur Spine J 2010 and Abbott & Schmitt JOSPT 2014 report smaller MCIDs in LBP — exact values UNVERIFIED from memory. Scoring behaviour verified in source.

things_done_right: Choosing a gravity-referenced phone inclinometer for ATR over the webcam is the single best measurement decision in the product; the code's rationale (no scale anchor, no projection, no model drift) is correct and the 'no_sensor is never zero' rule is exactly right.

The W3C axis choice itself is correct: with the phone flat across the back in portrait, beta is precisely the elevation of the long axis and therefore the trunk-rotation angle; there is no gimbal singularity near flat, so Euler angles are acceptable here.

Rejecting a reading rather than 'correcting' it, averaging over a window, requiring a minimum sample count, and stating 'the number and the threshold, never a diagnosis' are the right defaults; the 'main_thoracic: across the widest part of the rib hump' hint is apex-seeking, as a clinician would do.
atrPairsFrom() exists — the team already planned to MEASURE ATR repeatability instead of assuming the literature ICCs transfer. Keep that and ship it before any trend copy.

The MDC identities (SEM = SD_diff/√2, MDC95 = 1.96·SD_diff = 2.77·SEM) and Bland–Altman LoA are correct; sample SD with n−1 is right; bias is computed; describeDetectionLimit() copy ('changes smaller than X can't be told apart from noise, so we won't call them') is more honest than any consumer posture app.
METRICS_VERSION gating so version-1 and version-2 posture numbers are never pooled, and rotationVerified being null-not-zero, are exactly the discipline a measurement reviewer wants to see.
Weaker/stronger side-bridge ratio is a sensible direction-invariant summary for a mirrored-curve population; recording endedOnForm separately from failure is good practice.
PSFS and 'good days' as camera-free, patient-meaningful outcomes are the right feedback loop; the chosen PSFS constants are within the published convention.

Compensation cues require 2 s persistence and a 5 s refractory, visibility floors are applied before every geometric test, lunge pelvic tilt is explicitly declared out of scope, and birdDog normalises limb displacement by torso length — the right instinct that should be extended to every threshold.
Demoting the posture scan to qualitative and writing down its error budget (±20% torso length, yaw confound) was the correct call; the remaining task is just to make the UI match that decision.

evidence.headline: Balance has a genuinely good safety scaffold (red-flag gate, unknown-side withholding, honest ATR/MDC plumbing) but its exercise content overreaches its evidence: one Tier-3 side cue is anatomically reversed, the side-plank "contraindication" rests on a case series that failed replication, the product never tells a growing patient with Cobb >=20-25 deg that exercise is not a substitute for bracing, its ATR "refer at 7 deg" contradicts the HK school pathway it targets, and it is currently nowhere near the Yuan 2025 digital-PSSE comparator it is implicitly measured against.

findings.area: lib/exercises/library.ts — sitting_waist_fold (Tier 3) asymmetric_cues; also childs_pose_side_reach description
findings.claim_in_product: sitting_waist_fold, right_thoracic: "Fold to the left to open the right concave thoracic side."; left_thoracic: "Fold to the right to open the left concave thoracic side." Base description: "fold left waist (compresses left side, opens right)". childs_pose_side_reach: "Reach toward convex thoracic side to LENGTHEN it".
findings.problem: A right thoracic curve is convex to the right and concave on the LEFT — the library's own bird_dog and schroth_rotational_breathing entries say so ("opens the left concave side", "inhale into the left ribs"). sitting_waist_fold labels the concave side as RIGHT and instructs a lateral fold to the LEFT, which shortens the left (already collapsed) flank and opens the right (already long) convexity — the opposite of every scoliosis-specific school's elongate-the-concavity principle. This is a curve-worsening cue delivered as a 3x30s 'corrective' to exactly the patients it fits (right_thoracic, the most common AIS pattern). childs_pose_side_reach's action (reach right for right_thoracic = right side-bend = lengthens LEFT flank) is plausibly correct, but its rationale text ("lengthen the convex side") is anatomically wrong and will confuse any clinician reviewing the ruleset. The digest already flagged the internal inconsistency; this makes the direction of the error explicit.
findings.correction: Fix sitting_waist_fold now: right_thoracic -> "Fold to the RIGHT (toward the convex side) so the LEFT, concave flank lengthens"; left_thoracic -> fold LEFT; base description -> "lateral fold toward the convex side; the concave flank lengthens." Rewrite childs_pose_side_reach description to "reach toward the convex side so the concave flank lengthens" (keep the existing side cues). Add a unit test that asserts, for every side-dependent library entry, that the lengthened/opened side equals deriveRegionalSides().thoracicConcave, so a single convention is enforced across the library. Have a Schroth/SEAS-certified physiotherapist sign off every Tier-3 cue before it ships to anyone but the founder.
findings.evidence: Textbook convention: curve named by convexity; concavity is the opposite side (Weinstein & SRS nomenclature). Schroth/SEAS/BSPTS all correct by elongating the concave side and de-rotating the convex side (Weiss, Rigo; Romano SEAS). Internal evidence: library.ts lines 166-169 and 361-362 use the correct convention; lines 224 and 231-232 contradict them. Confidence high because the error is internal to the codebase and independent of any external source.

findings.area: Onboarding (CurveStep severity hints, OnboardingState.ageYears), selectProgram.ts self_guided mode, Coach prompt
findings.claim_in_product: Severity is captured as Mild "under 25°" / Moderate "25–40°" / Severe "over 40°" and age is captured, but neither gates anything except the left-thoracic red flag. The word "brace" does not appear anywhere in user-facing code. self_guided mode hands a 3–5 exercise programme to anyone, including a 13-year-old who selects "moderate" with no physio programme, with the note "consider booking a baseline assessment if you haven't."
findings.problem: SOSORT 2016 positions PSSE as first-line only for small curves in growing patients; for roughly Cobb 20–25 deg and above with growth remaining, bracing is the recommended treatment (with PSSE alongside it), and above ~45–50 deg surgery is considered. A home coach that silently accepts 'moderate (25–40°), age 14' and produces a programme functions as a bracing substitute by omission. The product also cannot coordinate PSSE-during-bracing (no brace-wear capture) even though that is a SOSORT-recommended combination. The team's roadmap explicitly targets HK school-screening adolescents, so this is not hypothetical.
findings.correction: Add a hard indication gate before any programme is produced: if ageYears < 18 (or skeletal maturity unknown) AND severity is moderate/severe OR parsed Cobb >= 20 deg, require the user to confirm they are under specialist/orthopaedic follow-up and show fixed copy: "For a growing spine with a curve of 20–25 degrees or more, guidelines recommend bracing be considered. Exercises here are meant to go alongside that care, not replace it." Capture brace status (yes/no, prescribed hours) and Risser/menarche/months-since-growth-spurt at onboarding; feed brace status to Coach so it schedules exercise in out-of-brace windows and never counts exercise as a reason to skip brace hours. In self_guided mode for anyone under 18, cap output to symmetric mobility/breathing (Tiers 4–5) and make the physio-programme path mandatory for anything asymmetric. Put the statement "Balance is not a substitute for bracing or surgery where those are indicated" in README 'Honest limits' and in WelcomeStep 'What I'm not'.
findings.evidence: Negrini S et al., 2016 SOSORT guidelines, Scoliosis Spinal Disord 2018;13:3 — 68 recommendations; bracing recommended for progressive curves during growth, PSSE recommended alongside bracing; secondary summaries of the guideline give observation <20 deg, observation-or-bracing 20–25, bracing 26–45, bracing-or-surgery 46–50, surgery >50 (from search snippets; the exact Risser-stratified practical-approach table could not be fetched — UNVERIFIED at the cell level, but the direction of the recommendation is not in doubt). Confidence high on the principle, medium on exact cut-points.

findings.area: lib/exercises/library.ts tiers 1–3; contraindications.ts (side_plank_wrong_side, deadlift, inversions); selectProgram.ts note "research-aligned additions"; tier label "Schroth-adjacent corrective"
findings.claim_in_product: Tier 3 is labelled "Schroth-adjacent corrective"; side_plank_convex_thoracic_side_down states "Wrong side held long is a contraindication" and checkSidePlankSide fires an ABSOLUTE rule: "Holding the other side reinforces the curve." physio_cleared mode calls Tier 1–2 suggestions "research-aligned additions". Deadlifts, inversions and long twists are listed as ABSOLUTE contraindications with mechanistic rationales ("amplify rotational forces", "stack asymmetric loads unpredictably").
findings.problem: The evidence status is not what the labels imply. (a) PSSE has moderate-quality RCT evidence for small Cobb effects only when delivered as a specific method (Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS) by trained therapists with 30–45 min/day home dose — nothing in Balance is a certified method, and 'Schroth' is a trademarked, certification-based term. (b) Tiers 1–2 (bridges, clams, lunges, bird-dog, squats, foam rolling) are generic core/hip work; there is no scoliosis-specific outcome evidence for them, and none at all for foam rolling/ITB in scoliosis. Calling them 'research-aligned' is unsupported. (c) The entire side-plank logic — convex side down, and the ABSOLUTE 'wrong side reinforces the curve' rule — descends from Fishman 2014, an uncontrolled case series (compliant AIS subgroup n=7), whose finding Sarkisova et al. 2019 could not replicate in a controlled study. There is no evidence that a side plank on the 'wrong' side worsens a curve; presenting it as an absolute contraindication is pseudo-precision that a clinician will spot immediately. (d) Deadlift/inversion/twist 'absolute' bans have no scoliosis evidence base; SOSORT's sport recommendations are permissive, and blanket bans for adults with stable curves reduce activity without benefit.
findings.correction: Add an evidence_status field to every Exercise and ContraindicationRule and render it: PSSE-method-derived (moderate evidence, requires trained therapist) | general conditioning (no scoliosis-specific outcome evidence; may help pain/endurance/function) | expert opinion. Rename Tier 3 to "Curve-specific positioning (physio-directed)" and remove 'Schroth' from any exercise not taught by a certified therapist; keep 'Schroth rotational breathing' only if renamed 'rotational breathing (Schroth-inspired)'. Downgrade side_plank_wrong_side from 'absolute' to 'ask_physio' with copy: "Some clinicians prefer a particular side for side planks; check which side your physio wants — the evidence either way is thin." Change "research-aligned additions" to "general conditioning your physio may or may not want to add". Move deadlift/inversion/twist to 'ask_physio' for adults; keep 'absolute' only for the emergency red-flag state. Label foam rolling explicitly as comfort/warm-up with no curve rationale, and drop the 'stiff hip flexor side' inference from 3-of-4 self-reported segment shifts unless a physio has confirmed it.
findings.evidence: Fishman LM, Groessl EJ, Sherman KJ. Serial case reporting yoga for idiopathic and degenerative scoliosis. Glob Adv Health Med 2014 (case series; ~40% Cobb reduction claimed, 23->11 deg in 7 compliant AIS). Sarkisova N, Andras LM, ... Skaggs DL. Side plank pose exercises for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients. Glob Adv Health Med 2019 — with a control group, no Cobb improvement in compliant patients; authors state the Fishman result could not be replicated. Schreiber S et al. 2015/2016 Schroth RCTs (Scoliosis; PLoS One) — effects with 1 h/week supervised + 30–45 min/day home Schroth, delivered by certified therapists. Negrini et al. SOSORT 2016: PSSE recommended as specific, therapist-delivered methods; generic physiotherapy not recommended as scoliosis treatment (UNVERIFIED wording — from memory of the guideline, full text could not be fetched). No published scoliosis outcome evidence for foam rolling or ITB release (absence of evidence — from memory, UNVERIFIED by search).

findings.area: app/monthly/page.tsx; README.md opening paragraph; lib/agents/prompts.ts Coach closing-line examples
findings.claim_in_product: monthly/page.tsx: "this is the same assessment physios use between X-rays to track curve progression. Capturing it monthly gives you clinically meaningful trend data" — attached to a webcam posture scan. README: the app "prescribes asymmetric exercises", "blocks contraindicated exercises", "tracks postural markers over time". Coach prompt sample outputs: "Three sessions in this week and your shoulder differential's already eased — that's the real win"; "same pattern other people on this curve have hit".
findings.problem: The team's own conclusion (lib/pose demotion, ±20% torso-length error, yaw confound) is that the webcam scan cannot measure Cobb or progression, yet the monthly page promises 'clinically meaningful trend data' on curve progression from it. 'Blocks contraindicated exercises' is false — physio_cleared mode flags and never blocks, and exerciseContraindicated() excludes nothing in the library. The Coach prompt trains the LLM to attribute short-term scan changes to exercise ('shoulder differential eased' after three sessions), which is an outcome claim the instrument cannot support, and 'other people on this curve have hit' asserts population evidence the product does not have. Honest claim space: adherence, self-reported pain, PSFS function, side-bridge/Sorensen endurance, ATR trend once its MDC is measured. Not claimable: Cobb reduction, progression prevention, curve 'correction'.
findings.correction: Rewrite monthly/page.tsx: "Forward-bend photos help you and your physio see the rib hump over time. They do not measure your curve angle — only an X-ray does that." Remove 'clinically meaningful'. README: replace 'prescribes' with 'guides', 'blocks' with 'flags', and add to Honest limits: "Balance does not reduce curve angle or prevent progression and does not claim to. What it can show: whether the exercise was done, how much, with what form, and how pain, function and endurance changed." In the Coach prompt, forbid attributing scan-metric changes to exercise and forbid any comparison to other patients; allow only adherence/pain/PSFS/endurance as 'wins'. Add a lint script (like scripts/check-safety.ts) that fails the build on the strings 'progression', 'correct your curve', 'clinically meaningful', 'reduce your curve' in user-facing files.
findings.evidence: Internal: lib/pose/* demotion notes and README 'Honest limits' contradict monthly/page.tsx copy; selectProgram.ts physioClearedMode flags only (line 56 comment: 'do not block; surface'); exerciseContraindicated() matches libraryIds that no rule carries. Clinical: only radiographic Cobb defines progression (>=5 deg change; the app's own redFlags.ts provenance line says so). Confidence high — internal consistency issue.

findings.area: selectProgram.ts (3–5 exercises, TARGET_COUNT_MIN/MAX), library.ts reps/sets/duration, Coach prompt rule 7 ("3 days focused + 4 lighter days"), trend.ts weekStats.totalMinutes
findings.claim_in_product: A daily session is 3–5 exercises at library defaults (e.g. 3x10 bridge, 3x30s side plank, 3x10 breaths). Coach prefers "3 days of focused practice + 4 lighter days". Nowhere is a minutes/day or days/week target stated to the user; totalMinutes is computed only retrospectively.
findings.problem: Every PSSE trial with a Cobb effect used a stated dose: Schreiber 2015/2016 — 1 h/week supervised plus 30–45 min/day home Schroth for 6 months; Yuan 2025 — 30 min/day, >=5 days/week, 6 months. A 3–5 exercise pick at library defaults is likely 10–15 minutes and the app never says so. Without a prescribed dose there is no denominator for adherence (see next finding), the Coach's 'deload/harder days' logic has nothing to anchor to, and any implicit curve benefit is being promised at a fraction of the studied dose. For adults with pain/function goals a lower dose is entirely reasonable — but it should be explicit.
findings.correction: Make dose a first-class field of the prescription: minutesPerDay and daysPerWeek, set by the physio programme when present, else user-chosen from labelled presets: "Maintenance (10–15 min, 3–4 days) — good for pain, stiffness, habit" and "Trial-level PSSE dose (30–45 min, 5–7 days) — the dose used in curve studies; only meaningful with a physio-prescribed programme". Show the estimated minutes of each generated session. Feed prescribed dose to Coach and forbid it from lowering below the physio's dose without a pain/red-flag reason. Store the prescription snapshot with each session so adherence can be computed against it.

findings.area: Whole product vs. Yuan et al. 2025 digital-PSSE RCT; docs/cuhk-approach.md positioning
findings.claim_in_product: The brief frames Balance as a digital home PSSE coach in the same space as the JAMA Netw Open 2025 trial ("−4.23° at 6 months"). findings.problem: Yuan et al. randomised 128 skeletally immature 9–17-year-olds to (a) PSSE (self-correction + overcorrection exercises) prescribed and supervised remotely by qualified physiotherapists through the Healbone Intelligent Rehabilitation System plus educational videos, or (b) 3 in-person physiotherapist sessions plus unsupervised home PSSE. Dose 30 min/day, >=5 days/week, 6 months. The −4.23° (95% CI −6.08 to −2.39; ITT) is the BETWEEN-GROUP difference in Cobb change, not the digital arm's absolute change — quoting it as 'reduced Cobb by 4.23°' misreads the result. Both arms received specialist-prescribed PSSE; the trial tests digital supervision of PSSE, not an app instead of a physio. Balance differs on every axis: population (adults), content (generic strength + unvalidated corrective cues), prescriber (algorithm or LLM in self_guided mode), dose (unspecified, likely a third), supervision (none — Liaison off), outcome (no radiographic endpoint). It is not a comparator today and should not be described as one.
findings.correction: State plainly in README and any pitch: "Balance is an adherence-and-coaching layer for physiotherapist-prescribed exercise; it is not a PSSE intervention and has no curve-outcome evidence." Lateral flexion to the left in a right-thoracic curve approximates the left (concave) ribs and lengthens the right (convex) side, i.e. it moves the trunk further into the deformity. Every PSSE school (Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS — Berdishevsky et al. 2016) corrects by elongating/opening the concavity, never by side-bending toward it. The left_thoracic cue is wrong in the mirror direction. Applicable_patterns is 'any', so the cue fires for every thoracic pattern. I could not find a reading under which this is correct; a self-guided user with no physio would be given a curve-reinforcing exercise. Critical is warranted. verdicts.reasoning: (a) Correct: the PSSE RCT evidence (Schreiber 2015 Scoliosis; 2016 PLoS One; Monticone 2014 SEAS; Kuru 2016) is method-specific, therapist-delivered, and with stated home dose; nothing in Balance is a certified method, and 'Schroth' is a protected/certification-based term in several jurisdictions, so 'Schroth-adjacent' is a hedge a clinician will notice. Downgrading to ask_physio is defensible; some Schroth-trained therapists do prescribe side-lying/side-plank positions by side, so 'check which side your physio wants' is the right copy. verdicts.note_for_author: All four sub-points hold. Fishman 2014 / Sarkisova 2019 characterisation is accurate. Mark the SOSORT 'generic exercise not recommended' wording as unverified.

verdicts.reasoning: The HK pathway description matches my knowledge of Fong et al. Spine 2010 and Luk et al. Downgrade to minor.

proposals.title: Prescribe → Verify → Report: the clinician-owned prescription as the product's spine
proposals.one_liner: Flip the product from a patient app that a physio occasionally receives a PDF from into a clinician-prescribed, dose-verified home-delivery instrument: the physio enters the prescription (exercises, sides, dose in minutes/day and days/week, red-flag disposition) in a 5-minute portal, the app delivers exactly that and nothing else, and the physio gets a between-visit ledger of verified minutes vs prescribed, pain/PSFS, apex ATR (MDC-gated) and any safety event — so the physio, not the patient, is the one who insists on it.
proposals.why_100x: Mechanism, not adjectives: (1) Distribution flips from B2C one-at-a-time to one clinician = every patient on their list. A PSSE physio or a scoliosis clinic carries 50-300 active patients; one adopting clinician is worth more than a year of consumer acquisition, and adherence to a clinician-mandated tool is far higher than to a self-downloaded coach. (2) It answers the one question every scoliosis clinician cannot answer today and cares about most: 'did they actually do the 30-45 min/day, and at what dose?' PSSE only shows Cobb effects in trials at a stated home dose (the digest cites Schreiber 2015/2016: 30-45 min/day; Yuan 2025: 30 min/day, 5+ days/week) and home adherence is the known failure point of the whole method; a physio who can see 'prescribed 210 min/week, verified 95, self-reported 160, side plank done 11 of 14 days' changes what they do at the next visit. That is workflow value, which is what makes a clinician write 'use Balance' on the prescription. (3) It structurally deletes the product's largest confirmed clinical-risk class. Nearly every critical finding in the audit (sitting_waist_fold backwards, 'lean side' laterality inversion, X-ray photo convexity flips, absolute-tier folk contraindications, invented cascades, no fusion/brace/maturity handling) exists because the product is guessing the clinician's decisions from lay input. When the physio states the pattern, the sides, the exercises, the dose, the fusion/brace/maturity status and their own contraindication list, the self-guided inference layer becomes a fallback for the unreferred adult, not the core. The clinician's stated convexity overrides self-report; the clinician's exercise list replaces the library's side-keying; the clinician's dose becomes the adherence denominator. (4) It makes the CUHK/trial claim true instead of aspirational: a prescription snapshot plus provenance-flagged adherence events (form_check_verified | timer_only | chat_self_report) is exactly the per-protocol denominator a trial statistician needs, which is the digest's own conclusion about what the 'trial that can finally tell whether the exercise was done' pitch requires. (5) It unlocks a payer: clinics and insurers/pilots pay for remote monitoring and adherence data; patients rarely pay for exercise reminders. The product stops being 'an exercise app for scoliosis' and becomes 'the delivery-and-verification layer for prescribed PSSE', which is a category with a buyer.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: Directly reusable: (a) physio_cleared mode in lib/exercises/selectProgram.ts already treats the physio programme as authoritative; it just needs to become the ONLY path when a clinician is linked, and to consume a structured prescription instead of regex on LLM-normalised names. (b) /api/parse-program + lib/prompts/parseProgram.ts already turns pasted text into a ParsedProgram mapped to library ids: this becomes the clinician's paste-to-prefill step (they confirm, not the patient). (c) The liaison agent + liaison_documents/appointments tables (app/api/agents/liaison/route.ts) already assemble a per-appointment handoff from observations; it becomes a weekly clinician-facing ledger rather than a one-off PDF. (d) lib/agents/context.ts AdherenceSnapshot, lib/session/persist.ts exercises_completed and the per-rep form scores in lib/exercises/formCheck/* give the raw material for a provenance-flagged adherence event; toolFlagSafety and lib/safety/redFlags.ts give the safety-event stream to surface to the clinician. (e) lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, side-bridge, Sorensen) and lib/pose/repeatability.ts (MDC machinery) plus lib/atr/compute.ts give the outcome columns; atrPairsFrom already collects the pairs the MDC gate needs. (f) app/care-team/page.tsx is a ready scaffold for a clinician dashboard (programs, observations, appointments, documents are already fetched). (g) Supabase auth and the privacy/redaction layer (lib/privacy, agents never see names) extend naturally to a clinician role with patient linking.
proposals.what_it_needs: Engineering: clinician role + consent-gated patient linking (invite code or QR at the visit); a Prescription object as first-class data (exerciseId or clinician's own free exercise, side enum left|right|both, sets/reps/seconds, minutesPerDay, daysPerWeek, clinician-stated curve pattern and convex sides, fusion/brace/maturity flags, clinician's own do-not-do list, valid-from/until) snapshotted weekly; adherence event schema with provenance and formScore, with weekly verified and reported adherence computed against the snapshot; clinician weekly ledger view + per-patient CSV export; clinician-owned exercise media (their own video or the library's) so Schroth/SEAS-certified physios are not forced into Balance's Tier-3 wording; hard rule that side-keyed library cues are withheld unless clinician-stated (kills the laterality problem); safety-event routing to the linked clinician with the existing condition-free copy; Traditional Chinese for both sides. Clinical: 2-3 design-partner PSSE physios (HK and one Schroth/SEAS-certified clinic) to co-design the 5-minute prescription flow; a clinician sign-off on every remaining self-guided cue (the audit's ask) so the fallback path is not a liability that scares clinicians away from the linked path. Data: fix the denominator first (prescribed dose stored), then instrument verified vs reported minutes; expect form-check-verified to be honest only for side plank sag and rep counting per the biomech audit, so the primary verified signal is timer-on-exercise-screen plus rep count, labelled as such. Partnerships: CUHK orthopaedics/physio (docs/cuhk-approach.md already points here) for a monitoring-arm pilot; a HK physio association or two private scoliosis clinics as the first paying accounts. Regulatory/ethics: once a clinician relies on the ledger it is a clinical decision-support tool; expect PDPO data-processing agreements with clinics, an REB submission for the CUHK arm, and to keep all claims to adherence/pain/function/endurance (never curve change) so it stays in the lowest software-as-medical-device risk tier.
proposals.biggest_risk: Clinician non-adoption due to friction and liability, producing a two-sided cold start where neither side has data. Concretely: a physio will not type a prescription into a fourth system for no fee, and a physio who does will stop if the ledger creates alarms they must act on (a red-flag event at 9pm, a 'below prescribed dose' banner) without a reimbursement or workflow slot to absorb it. The second-order failure is that if the 'verified' signal degrades to timer-only (which the biomech audit says is likely for most exercises from a single webcam), the ledger is only modestly more trustworthy than a paper diary, and a sceptical clinician will discount it; if that happens the product has spent its runway building a portal for a signal clinicians do not believe. Mitigations, not guarantees: paste-to-prefill so the prescription takes under 5 minutes; default ledger is weekly digest with no interruptive alerts except the emergency tier; label verified vs reported honestly from day one; run the first pilot inside a clinic that already wants adherence data for a study, so the clinician's motive is the trial, not the app.
proposals.evidence_basis: High confidence (verified in code today): physio_cleared mode flags and never blocks; exerciseContraindicated() excludes nothing; /api/parse-program sends raw pasted text to Groq and matches against libraryForPrompt(); the liaison route generates a per-appointment PDF from unconsumed observations; app/care-team is an admin view with no clinician auth; no Prescription/dose object exists, so adherence has no denominator; exercises_completed mixes chat self-report and camera-verified entries with no provenance (per the evidence audit). High confidence (confirmed audit): nearly all critical/major clinical findings stem from lay-inferred sides, patterns and contraindications that a clinician could state directly. Medium confidence: the trial dose figures (Schreiber 2015/2016 30-45 min/day; Yuan 2025 30 min/day, 5+ days/week) and the 'adherence = delivered/prescribed, often >=80% per-protocol' convention are taken from the embedded digest and my clinical training; I did not re-verify the papers against a source in this run. Medium-to-low confidence: the claim that clinicians will mandate a tool that shows verified dose is an inference from PSSE practice (home dose is the known weak link) and from adjacent remote-therapeutic-monitoring products, not from user interviews with HK scoliosis physios; the panel-size and adoption multipliers are order-of-magnitude reasoning, not measured. Low confidence: regulatory tiering and any payer willingness in HK were not checked against current HK MDD or insurer guidance.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 6-8 weeks to a minimal linked mode with 2-3 design-partner physios: clinician magic-link login, paste-to-prefill prescription with sides and dose, self-guided path disabled for linked patients, weekly ledger (verified vs reported minutes, pain, PSFS, red-flag events) as a web page plus the existing PDF, CSV export. The first 'value moment' is the first follow-up visit where a physio changes a plan because of the ledger, realistically 3-4 weeks after the first patient is linked, so about 3 months from start. A CUHK monitoring-arm pilot with MDC-gated ATR and ICC on the adherence signal is 6-9 months and depends on REB timing.

proposals.title: Recorded With Your Physio: the patient's own supervised session becomes the programme, and the physio sees it happen
proposals.one_liner: At the appointment, the physio uses Balance to film the patient doing each exercise correctly under their hands (patient's own body, correct side, physio's voice cue, dose); that capture replaces the generic library as the home programme, each home session is verified against the patient's own clinic reference, and the physio gets a 30-second weekly view with a one-tap reply — so at week 26 the patient is still doing "my exercises, that my physio watches", not "an app's exercises".
proposals.why_100x: Three mechanisms, all about what kills adherence at week 6-10 for a scoliosis patient. (1) Fidelity: PSSE is individualised per curve and patients forget or drift the cues within days of leaving clinic; a paper handout or a generic library cannot encode "your left scapula, your right pelvis, that much breath". A video of the patient's own body in the corrected position, with the physio's own voice saying the cue they used in the room, is the highest-fidelity home prescription possible and needs no side-inference at all — laterality is baked in by the clinician who positioned the patient. This deletes at one stroke the entire class of audited harms (sitting_waist_fold inverted, bulge/lean self-report, X-ray laterality flips, invented hip-flexor rule, cascade chains): in this mode the product never has to decide which side is concave. (2) Accountability with a face: the strongest known lever on home-exercise adherence is feedback from the treating clinician, not gamification or an LLM persona. The retention engine becomes "my physio saw Tuesday's session and said 'good, hold the breath longer'". The Companion nudges become the physio's words, delivered by the app. (3) It changes who the customer is and what the product IS: from a consumer coach with a library a clinician distrusts, to the fidelity-and-adherence infrastructure of an existing clinical relationship. The buyer becomes the PSSE clinic (in HK, certified Schroth physios are scarce, private, seen roughly monthly, and currently hand out paper) and the trial group (CUHK's exact unmet need per docs/cuhk-approach.md: objective adherence to a therapist-defined prescription — now with the prescription itself captured as the reference, so 'did they do what was prescribed, how well' is finally answerable). Every physio who adopts brings all their scoliosis patients; the physio, not the founder, does the acquisition and the safety sign-off. Self-guided mode shrinks to a symmetric mobility/breathing fallback, which is the only place the current library is defensible anyway.
