proposals.what_it_needs: Engineering: clinician account + patient-link consent + RLS policies; an in-clinic capture flow that takes under 8 minutes for a 5-exercise programme (per exercise: 15-30s video, 10s voice cue, side, sets/reps/seconds; one tap to save) with encrypted storage and retention rules; home-session playback of the patient's own clip as the reference (side-by-side or ghost overlay); form-check refactor to compare against the personal clinic reference instead of fixed thresholds, with the 'theatre' checks removed; adherence event schema with provenance; a physio weekly digest (one screen: adherence vs prescribed dose, pain, ATR at the known apex level, form flags) with one-tap replies ('keep going', 'longer hold', 'come in early') and a voice-note reply; a 'your physio saw this' marker on the patient side. Clinical: two or three certified Schroth/SEAS physios as design partners to co-author the capture flow and the digest, and to sign off that a filmed-in-clinic reference is acceptable as the home prescription; a defined escalation path so the red-flag screen routes to the named physio, not only to a PDF. Data/ethics: video of patients' backs (including minors) — HK PDPO compliance, guardian consent and child assent, retention and deletion policy, data-minimisation statement; a small before/after study of week-12 and week-26 adherence against the current library path. Partnerships: one HK private physio clinic for the paid pilot (billable 'between-visit monitoring'), and the CUHK PWH physiotherapy group as the trial-instrument route already sketched in docs/cuhk-approach.md.
proposals.biggest_risk: The physio does not spend the minutes. Capture adds time to an appointment that already runs over, and the weekly review is unpaid work; if the physio stops looking, the patient discovers within two weeks that nobody is watching, and the accountability mechanism inverts — a 'seen by your physio' promise that goes unmet is worse for week-26 retention than no promise at all. This is a business-model risk as much as a UX one: it works only where monitoring is billable (private HK clinics) or funded (a trial), and the digest must be genuinely 30 seconds with a one-tap reply, or it dies. Secondary risks: filming adolescents' backs raises safeguarding and body-image issues that the current product does not yet handle (no age capture, no guardian consent — see the safety_informatics findings), and any patient without a physio still falls back to the generic library, so the audited library and laterality fixes remain mandatory, not superseded.
proposals.evidence_basis: Confidence by claim. HIGH: PSSE methods (Schroth, SEAS, BSPTS) are individualised to curve pattern and delivered by trained therapists, and the only trials with Cobb effects used that supervised, method-specific delivery (Schreiber 2015/2016 as already cited in the evidence audit); a clinician-positioned reference removes the app's need to infer laterality, which is the root of the critical library and profile findings. MEDIUM (from general physiotherapy literature, not scoliosis-specific, and not re-verified against sources in this run): home-exercise adherence falls off within weeks and is over-reported by diaries; feedback and supervision from the treating clinician are among the strategies most consistently associated with better adherence in reviews of physiotherapy home-programme adherence; patients recall prescribed exercises poorly and video-based instruction improves performance accuracy over paper handouts. MEDIUM: certified Schroth physiotherapists in Hong Kong are few and private, with roughly monthly visits — from domain familiarity, not a counted source. LOW/UNTESTED: that a physio will reliably review a weekly digest — no evidence in the codebase or literature I can cite; this is precisely the pilot's primary hypothesis. Internal evidence: docs/cuhk-approach.md already identifies objective adherence to a therapist-defined prescription as the product's only genuinely differentiated asset; this feature is the shortest path to making that claim true.
proposals.time_to_first_value: 4-6 weeks for the founder-and-her-own-physio pilot: physio films the exercises on a phone in clinic, the app plays the patient's own clip as the session reference with timer and hold, no form-check, physio receives the existing Liaison digest re-cut as a weekly note. 2-3 months for the clinician role, capture flow and one-tap reply with two partner physios and 10-20 patients. A first retention read (week-12 adherence, recorded-with-physio vs library path) at about 5-6 months; the week-26 answer at about 8 months. The CUHK conversation can begin as soon as the capture plus provenance-tagged adherence export exist, roughly month 3.

proposals.title: Trial Mode: a locked-prescription, dose-denominated, provenance-tagged adherence instrument with statistician-grade export
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from a coach that prescribes into an instrument that measures: the clinician's PSSE prescription becomes a versioned, signed object; every set is logged as an adherence event with prescribed-vs-completed dose and a source tag (form-check-verified | timer-only | chat-self-report); the LLM coach, self-guided programme generator, cascade models and scan-trend language are switched OFF in this mode; and the whole thing exports as a pseudonymised per-participant table with a data dictionary a trial statistician can drop into a per-protocol analysis.
proposals.why_100x: The multiplier is a change of buyer and a change of what the artefact is worth per user. Today the product's value per user is one patient's exercise habit, and the audit shows that as a prescriber it is currently net-negative (backwards waist-fold cue, invented cascades, a contraindication engine that flags physio programmes and blocks nothing). As a trial instrument, value per user is a fraction of the cost of the trial it makes interpretable: every PSSE RCT (Schreiber-style, 6 months, 30-45 min/day home dose) has the same unsolved confound - if the exercise arm underperforms nobody can say whether the exercise failed or was not done, because adherence is a paper diary. docs/cuhk-approach.md already names this as "the only part of this product genuinely ahead of what a research group could commission" but the code does not deliver it: exercises_completed has no denominator, no timestamps per set, mixes chat self-report with camera-verified reps, and the prescription is never snapshotted. Mechanism, step by step: (1) a locked prescription gives adherence a denominator, so weekly adherence = verified minutes / prescribed minutes exists for the first time; (2) the source tag lets a statistician run per-protocol analysis on verified dose and sensitivity analysis on reported dose - that is the analysis nobody in PSSE research can currently run, and it yields the first dose-response data in the field; (3) switching off every prescribing/coaching component in Trial Mode converts the audit's liabilities into non-issues (the physio's prescription is authoritative, the app adds no co-intervention that would confound the trial arm) and drops the regulatory posture from "software that prescribes exercise" to "software that records exercise"; (4) a trial that designs the instrument into its protocol produces a peer-reviewed paper citing it, which is the validation every clinician demands before recommending it to patients - so the research angle is also the only credible route back to the consumer/clinic market; (5) the same ledger, once a few hundred patient-years exist, is the longitudinal behaviour-plus-pain-plus-ATR dataset the roadmap's TOCI/progression conversation needs. One instrument, three markets (trials, PSSE clinics, then patients), and the trial market pays in credibility rather than cash, which is what this product is actually short of.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on: lib/session/persist.ts already writes a Supabase sessions row keyed by profile_id with started_at/completed_at/pain_check/exercises_completed - the ledger is an expansion of exerciseSummaries into per-set events, not a new pipeline. lib/exercises/formCheck/* produce per-rep form scores and compensation events that are computed but never persisted; the rep counters for hip bridge/lunge and the side-plank hold timer are the pieces the biomech audit rates PLAUSIBLE, which is exactly what "verified" should be built on. lib/prompts/parseProgram.ts + selectProgram physio_cleared mode already ingest a pasted physio programme with source_text - that is the prescription object, missing only versioning, sets/reps/minutes-per-day/days-per-week fields, a clinician signature and a lock. lib/pose/repeatability.ts has SEM/MDC95/Bland-Altman and buildMdcTable, and lib/atr atrPairsFrom collects test-retest pairs - the instrument's own reliability study is mostly written. lib/outcomes/compute.ts (PSFS, Sorensen, side-bridge L/R) are the secondary outcomes a trial would want alongside adherence. lib/agents/tools.ts log_exercise already writes to exercises_completed with a source column ("real") - the provenance enum slots straight in. scripts/check-safety.ts is the pattern for a build-time lint that fails Trial Mode if any prescribing/trend copy leaks. lib/safety/redFlags.ts is the adverse-event screen an ethics committee will ask for. docs/cuhk-approach.md is the pitch; the feature makes its one-sentence claim true.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (8-12 weeks for a shippable v1): adherence event schema {participantId(pseudonymous), exerciseId, prescriptionVersion, startedAt, endedAt, prescribedSets/reps/seconds, completedSets/reps/seconds, source enum, formScore 0-1|null, compensationEvents[], deviceId, appVersion, rulesetHash}; versioned prescription table with clinician id, signature timestamp and lock; Trial Mode feature flag that disables self_guided selection, Coach/Companion nudges, cascade.ts, posture-scan mm/trend output and all curve-change copy; weekly adherence computation with verified and reported figures; CSV/Parquet export + data dictionary + audit log, REDCap-importable; site dashboard for missing-data and device-failure monitoring; raise MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC to 10 with CI-adjusted MDC and add ICC(2,1) per the biomech audit; the deterministic safety pre-filter and timestamped safety-answer log from the safety_informatics findings (an ethics committee will require the adverse-event pathway to work). CLINICAL: one PSSE-certified physiotherapist to own the prescription editor and sign off any cue text that remains visible (Tier-3 content must be fixed or removed before any patient sees it in a trial); a supervised-observation validation study (n~20-30, therapist-observed home sessions vs app-logged verified minutes; home-helper phone-ATR test-retest vs clinician scoliometer) - this is the paper that makes the instrument citable. DATA/GOVERNANCE: pseudonymisation at the edge, HK PDPO compliance, CUHK-NTEC CREC ethics submission, data-ownership terms conceded to the study upfront (as cuhk-approach.md recommends), parental consent and child assent in Traditional Chinese and English for any under-18 arm, guardian/clinician gating for minors. PARTNERSHIPS: a CUHK O&T researcher planning the successor to NCT03427970 (or any SOSORT-affiliated PSSE group - the instrument is trial-agnostic), a PSSE clinic for the validation pilot, and a biostatistician to co-author the data dictionary so the export is built to the analysis, not the other way round. Resolve HSBC IP and tag the repo first, per the existing checklist.
proposals.biggest_risk: That "verified" is not verification. The biomech audit rates most single-webcam checks as theatre (hip-height cues, spine rotation, press-down side), and what survives - rep counts, hold timers, side-plank sag - can confirm a body moved in roughly the right way for roughly the right time, not that the prescribed corrective was performed with the prescribed asymmetry or effort. If the validation study shows verified minutes disagree materially with therapist-observed sessions (wrong exercise counted, half-effort holds counted, two-person or off-camera sessions not counted), the instrument collapses to a timestamped diary and the whole premise of the pitch fails in front of the one audience that will check. Mitigation is to define "verified" narrowly and honestly (presence + matched movement pattern + duration, with formScore reported separately and never inflated), publish the agreement statistics before making the claim, keep timer_only and self_report as first-class categories rather than hiding them, and let the trial's own supervised sessions calibrate the home logs. Secondary risks: the app itself becomes a co-intervention (reminders, feedback) that confounds the exercise arm unless Trial Mode is genuinely stripped or randomised as a factor; and NCT03427970 may already be complete, so the timing depends on a successor protocol and a grant cycle the founder does not control.
proposals.evidence_basis: HIGH confidence (verified in repo): persist.ts writes exercises_completed with no denominator, no per-set timestamps, no provenance; tools.ts log_exercise writes chat self-report into the same field; repeatability.ts implements SEM/MDC95/Bland-Altman with a 5-pair gate; parseProgram.ts ingests physio programmes with source_text; docs/cuhk-approach.md frames adherence measurement as the sole differentiator and names NCT03427970 as primary target. HIGH confidence (confirmed audit findings supplied): the adherence and dose findings (evidence/major, evidence/minor) that no prescribed dose or provenance exists; biomech triage of which form checks are plausible vs theatre; safety_informatics findings that the ongoing safety screen is dead code and that no age gate exists. MEDIUM confidence (from the digest, not independently re-verified here): PSSE trial doses (Schreiber 2015/2016 ~30-45 min/day home plus weekly supervised; Yuan 2025 30 min/day, >=5 days/week, 6 months) and the ">=80% per-protocol" adherence convention - consistent with my clinical recollection but no source was fetched in this run. LOW confidence: current recruitment status of NCT03427970 and whether a successor protocol exists - unverified; the plan should not depend on that specific trial. No numeric claims about trial cost or market size are made because none could be sourced.
proposals.time_to_first_value: ~6 weeks to the research-conversation deliverable: adherence event schema, a locked prescription object, a sample pseudonymised export with data dictionary, and a written validation protocol - enough to walk into a CUHK O&T researcher's office with something a statistician can critique. 8-12 weeks to a usable Trial Mode build (ledger, provenance, coaching stripped, export, minors gating). ~3 months after that for the supervised-observation validation pilot that makes "verified adherence" a defensible claim. First trial participant enrolled on the instrument: 6-18 months, governed by ethics approval and the partner's protocol/grant cycle rather than by engineering.

proposals.title: The Watch Window: a clinician-shared observation ledger for HK's observed-but-untreated cohort
proposals.one_liner: Turn Balance from an adult exercise coach into the between-visit monitoring record for every HK schoolchild who screened positive but is only being "observed" — a per-child ledger of helper-measured ATR at the known apex (gated on the child's own repeatability), height velocity and maturity milestones, brace-window status, and PSSE adherence — that the Student Health Service / Special Assessment Centre or orthopaedic clinic receives as a one-page summary at each 6–12-month review, with exercises demoted to an adjunct module inside it.
proposals.why_100x: Mechanism, not adjectives: (1) Cohort size and structure. If ~2.8% of screened students are referred and ~9% of those need treatment, then ~91% of referrals — roughly 2.5% of all screened students, i.e. ~10x the treated group — are placed in watchful waiting. Nobody owns that interval today: the child is seen every 6–12 months, and between visits the family has no instrument, no record, and no way to know whether to come back early. The product that owns the interval owns the cohort. (2) Buyer changes from individual to institution. An exercise coach is sold one adult at a time; an observation ledger is a pathway component that SHS/SAC or a hospital ortho clinic wants for every observed child, because it answers the one question their 6-monthly visit cannot: what happened in the gap. That converts consumer churn into a per-cohort, per-year institutional relationship (and is exactly the "between-visit monitoring, not screening" position docs/cuhk-approach.md already reaches — but never encodes as product). (3) It is the only cohort where the product's exercise content is actually indicated. SOSORT positions PSSE as first-line specifically for small curves in growing patients — which is the definition of the observed cohort. For adults with fixed curves the coach promises pain/function; for observed adolescents it is the guideline-recommended intervention, delivered where it must happen (home) with the adherence provenance the CUHK pitch depends on. (4) The data asset compounds. Longitudinal home ATR at the apex + height velocity + menarche/Risser + adherence + pain, on thousands of observed children, is the input that progression-prediction work (the "three-year conversation" TOCI line in the CUHK doc) does not have. The ledger makes that dataset a by-product of routine care rather than a study you have to fund. (5) It converts the product's honesty into the differentiator. The whole audit says the product cannot claim curve change; a ledger's job is not to claim change but to bring a repeatability-gated reading, a growth spurt flag, and a brace-window prompt to the clinician on time. "Book your SAC visit sooner — your helper readings moved more than your own noise floor and you grew 4 cm in 5 months" is a claim the instrument CAN support, and it is worth more to a family and a clinic than any exercise.
proposals.what_exists_to_build_on:
- lib/atr/compute.ts: captureAtr, TRUNK_LEVELS, summarise, atrPairsFrom — the phone-inclinometer ATR and the same-day pair collector; needs the audit fixes (apex-from-report as primary site, sweep mode, orientation confirmation, per-level trend, drop 7° band) but the instrument and the repeatability hook exist.
- lib/pose/repeatability.ts: computeRepeatability / buildMdcTable / describeDetectionLimit — the per-user MDC machinery that makes "changed vs noise" an honest statement; raise MIN_PAIRS_FOR_MDC per the biomech finding and it is the ledger's core gate.
- lib/safety/redFlags.ts three-tier triage + condition-free copy style — the vehicle for the new adolescent items (juvenile onset, painful curve, apex hyperkyphosis, brace-window REVIEW flag).
- Physio handoff PDF + Gemini X-ray REPORT parsing (confirm-per-field) — repurpose the report parser to ingest the SAC/orthopaedic letter (Cobb, apex, convex side, Risser) and the PDF to become the clinic-facing "since last visit" summary.
- selectProgram.ts physio_cleared mode — the mandatory path for minors; the ledger's exercise module is physio_cleared only, capped to Tiers 4–5 when no prescription exists.
- Outcomes module (PSFS, pain days) and the adherence event schema proposed in the evidence findings — the adherence half of the ledger.
- docs/cuhk-approach.md — the institutional route (adherence sub-study with CUHK O&T; between-visit ATR positioning) is already written; this feature is what makes that document a product rather than a pitch.
proposals.what_it_needs: ENGINEERING (~3 months to a pilotable build, given the audit fixes are prerequisite): (a) ship the ATR fixes (apex-keyed primary site, sweep/max mode, orientation confirmation, zero-offset, 4 s median window, per-level trend, MDC gate at ≥10 pairs with conservative bound); (b) new profile fields: date of birth, sex, menarche status/date, self-measured height log (monthly), Risser/Cobb/apex from clinic letter, brace status and prescribed hours, next scheduled review date; (c) a growth-velocity computation (cm/yr from height log) and a deterministic "bring forward your visit" rule set — ATR change > personal MDC at apex, height velocity above a clinician-set threshold during the immature window, new pain, any red flag — that never emits "stable"; (d) guardian consent + child assent flow, minors default to no LLM chat/no Companion nudges, no scan-derived body numbers; (e) a clinic-facing one-page PDF/CSV per child per interval and a clinic dashboard listing observed children by review-due date and open flags; (f) Traditional Chinese throughout (helper is a parent). CLINICAL: a paediatric spine orthopaedic surgeon and a certified PSSE physiotherapist to set the bring-forward thresholds and sign the exercise tiers permitted for minors; a clinical hazard analysis with the false-reassurance hazard named. DATA: a same-day ATR pair at enrolment plus one at every clinic visit (clinician-measured scoliometer alongside) to establish helper-vs-clinician agreement — this is the validation study and it is small. PARTNERSHIPS: one orthopaedic clinic's observation arm (CUHK O&T via the sub-study framing, or a private paediatric spine clinic) as the pilot; the Department of Health SHS is the eventual counterparty but must not be approached with an unvalidated instrument, and the school cohort must never be recruited through schools without DH. REB: parental consent and child assent in Chinese and English, data-minimisation for minors, named escalation clinician.
proposals.biggest_risk: False reassurance that costs a child the bracing window. ATR–Cobb correlation is only moderate; a curve can progress radiographically while a parent-placed phone at four levels reads flat, and a family holding a ledger of "nothing moved" is exactly the family that skips or defers the SAC visit — the one outcome that makes the product net-harmful. This is compounded by the helper's laterality and level-placement error, and by the institutional risk that a private app sitting alongside the DH pathway is seen as a parallel screener (the comparison the CUHK doc already says you lose). Mitigations must be designed in, not bolted on: the ledger only ever emits "keep your scheduled visit" or "bring it forward"; it never emits reassuring language; the scheduled-review date is a hard field and the product nags toward it; every summary carries "only an X-ray measures your curve"; growth velocity and maturity — not ATR — drive the brace-window prompt. If the team cannot commit to a product that is forbidden to say "stable", it should not build this.
proposals.evidence_basis: Confidence notes (sources not re-fetched this run; figures from memory and from the supplied digest): HIGH — the HK pathway shape: SHS screens students annually from around Primary 5, refers ATR 5–14° to moiré/periodic re-screen and ATR ≥15° or ≥2 moiré lines to radiograph (Luk et al. 2010, Spine; Fong et al. 2015, Spine J) — exact cut-offs to be verified before copy ships, as the digest already requires. MEDIUM — the ~2.8% referral / ~9% needing treatment figures are as given in the brief; the derived "observed ≈ 10x treated" follows arithmetically and is the load-bearing claim; the absolute cohort size (tens of thousands of HK children under observation at any time) is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a verified number. HIGH — SOSORT 2016 guidelines (Negrini et al. 2018) recommend PSSE for small curves in growing patients and bracing from roughly 20–25° with growth remaining; BrAIST (Weinstein et al. 2013, NEJM) established bracing efficacy, which is why the window matters. MEDIUM — peak height velocity / growth spurt and Risser/menarche as progression predictors are standard (Lonstein & Carlson 1984; Sanders et al.), but I have not verified specific velocity thresholds and the product should take them from its clinical advisors. MEDIUM — helper-measured scoliometer agreement with clinicians is not established (the digest's biomech finding); the enrolment-visit pairing is the proposed fix and is unproven. HIGH (from repo) — docs/cuhk-approach.md already positions ATR as between-visit monitoring and names CUHK NCT03427970/NCT03904914; repeatability and pair-collection code exists in lib/pose/repeatability.ts and lib/atr/compute.ts.
proposals.time_to_first_value: First value to a family: at the second same-day ATR pair (enrolment + first repeat), i.e. within the first clinic interval — the child gets a personal noise floor and a "bring this to your visit" summary instead of nothing. First value to a clinic: the first review cycle after pilot start (~6 months), when the clinician receives between-visit summaries for an observation-arm caseload. Build time: ~3 months of engineering after the prerequisite audit fixes (ATR, minors gate, library convention) plus REB approval running in parallel (~3–6 months in HK); realistic first pilot data at 9–12 months, and the institutional (DH/SHS) conversation only after a clinic pilot has shown helper-vs-clinician agreement.
